entries.title: Gateway won't start: the port is already taken
entries.title_zh: 网关起不来：端口被占用
entries.symptom: Port 5476 already in use — is another Kiro Crew gateway running?
entries.trust_note: Human-confirmed across several reports. The common root cause is a leftover old gateway, or a local gateway and a tunnel fighting over the port. your previous tool used 7777; Kiro Crew defaults to 5476.

steps.expect: "Gateway stopped".
Either "Gateway stopped" or "No gateway running" is OK. This clears a gateway on the older default port.
steps.t: Stop anything holding the old port
steps.t_zh: 停止占用旧端口的进程

steps.do: Start again with `kirocrew gateway`.
steps.expect: No output means the port is free.

if_stuck.note:
1. **Service points at old install** — If the port is free but it still won't start, your service may point at an old install. The service can default to port `7777` (colliding with an old your previous tool gateway) instead of `5476`: Kiro Crew's real default port is `5476`, and `7777` is a stale value carried over from your previous tool. Set the stored port back to `5476`, or stop the old your previous tool gateway that is still running.
2. **Non-KiroCrew process holds port** — If the logs say the port is held by a non-KiroCrew process and it 'refused to terminate it': Kiro Crew reclaims the port from a stale Kiro Crew gateway but deliberately will not kill a process that is not its own. Find and kill it yourself with `lsof -i :7777` then `kill <PID>`, and retry.
3. **Gateway lock already held** — 'lock is held by another pid that already owns `~/.kiro/crew` and holds port `5476`' is not an error, it is a guardrail: a gateway is already running and holding the lock, so a second instance refuses to start. Just open the http://localhost URL it printed.
4. **No gateway running message** — If it says "No gateway running", continue anyway.

entries.crew_prompt: My kirocrew gateway won't start and says port 5476 is already in use. Do not kill anything unrelated.

entries.crew_prompt: I'm not sure which model/provider to use (Kiro ACP vs Claude Code vs Bedrock). Please explain the tradeoffs briefly, help me set one in Settings, and send a short test message to confirm it responds on my machine. Note: this guidance is unverified reference, not a confirmed answer.

if_stuck.note:
1. **No provider-picker page** — There is no provider-picker page: in this build the provider is pinned to the Kiro/acp engine, so switching provider in `config.json` or Settings is a dead end. A provider-picker UI is still in progress.
2. **Use Claude Code backend** — To use Claude Code you run `kirocrew config set agent.acp_backend claude_code` (you also need `npm install @agent-client-protocol/claude-agent-acp` and `claude` on PATH), then restart the gateway. (The Amazon internal edition additionally honours a `KIROCREW_PROVIDER=claude_code` env override; the public edition does not read it.)
3. **Models suddenly missing** — A model (or a lot of them, e.g. `GPT 5.6`) suddenly missing from the model list is usually a network hiccup while fetching the list: stop and restart Kiro Crew to restore it, the model was not removed.
4. **Opus silently downgrades** — Setting the default model to `Opus 4.8` under Claude Code but still running `Opus 4.6` (silent downgrade at startup) is a known race where the toolbox claude wrapper rewrites cc-config on every spawn: select `4.8` at runtime in the session instead (runtime selection works; it just does not stick as a startup default).
5. **Provider errors on switch** — If it errors, try another provider

entries.crew_prompt: My Kiro Crew fails with 'Request session/new timed out' / 'AcpRuntime dead (PID): killed'. Root cause: a full agent loads ~74 MCP servers and exceeds the session-start budget, which defaults to 90s (a separate, larger budget than the 30s per-request timeout), so the subprocess is SIGKILLed. The real fix is to raise `agent.session_start_timeout_secs` (e.g. 180) in config.json / Settings; alternatively trim MCP servers in Settings → MCP, then restart and start a fresh session. This is a known limitation, not my misconfiguration.

if_stuck.note:
1. **Handshake stalls during startup** — Both 'AcpRuntime dead ... killed [returncode=None]' and 'session/new timed out': almost always a single MCP server exiting silently (rc=0, empty stderr) during handshake and stalling startup. Run `kirocrew --verbose gateway` (note: `-vv` raises logging to DEBUG) to see which server it hangs on, then disable it in Settings then MCP.
2. **macOS spawn-kill during handshake** — On macOS when the traceback path is `/Users/...`, the root cause is almost always a bad kiro-cli version (`2.18.x/2.19.x/2.20.1` spawn-kill during the `30s` ACP handshake); upgrade or pin kiro-cli to a good version.
3. **Open sessions keep old MCP** — MCP is injected at session creation and reloading an open session will not apply: open a brand-new chat, or inside the session do `/agentswap <other>` then `/agentswap kirocrew` to force an MCP rebuild, then confirm with `/tools`.
4. **Context truncation is not crash** — A 'Session context too large (NNNNN chars), truncating to `165000`' warning is NOT a crash — Kiro Crew is trimming oldest history to stay in budget.
5. **Session context grows too large** — A session bloats from too many MCP servers enabled at once (each loads its full tool schema every turn; builder-mcp alone ~1/4 of the window), one huge tool payload, pasting large content, or a long thread never compacted. Start a fresh session per task (each dashboard tab and Slack thread is its own isolated session), disable unused MCP servers in `mcp.json` and restart, and reference files with `#File` instead of pasting.

entries.title: Add a team's external app registry
entries.title_zh: 添加团队的外部 app registry
entries.symptom: Your team has a self-hosted app registry and you want its apps to appear in the App Store.

steps.do: Go to Apps → Discover and click the Sources gear.
steps.expect: The panel lists app sources and an 'Add registry' form for name, repo, and branch.
steps.t: Open the App Store Sources menu
steps.t_zh: 打开 App Store Sources 菜单

steps.do: Fill in name (e.g. my-team), repo (the git-cloneable URL like https://github.com/my-team/AppRegistry), and branch (main), then click Add. `repo` MUST be a git-cloneable URL. Confirm, since you're the one choosing to pull its apps.
steps.expect: A bare package name or an internal branch like `mainline` is rejected as non-cloneable. Adding a host also asks you to trust it once. The index is read as app-registry.json at the repo root, falling back to auto-discovering apps/*/app.json when no index file exists.

steps.do: So the store re-fetches. Click the Refresh button in the Discover header.
steps.do_zh: 让商店重新拉取。
steps.expect: The external index is otherwise cached for 1 hour. The new source appears with its apps. Note the SOURCE count shows only NOT-yet-installed apps, so an already-installed app is excluded — a count of 0 can be normal, not a failure.

steps.do: Keep the configured URL byte-identical; changing ssh://host/x vs ssh://user@host/x or a trailing .git silently drops apps back to anonymous.
steps.expect: A plain external registry uses the default 'index' trust tier: its apps clone credential-free — an anonymous git env plus a sandbox that hides ~/.ssh — so the registry repo and every app it lists must be readable without your credentials (that is why the example above is a public URL). Two cases clone WITH your machine's git identity instead: the same-repo carve-out (an app whose clone URL is byte-identical to the registry `repo` you configured — the monorepo layout, apps under apps/*/), and a registry your deployment has pinned as owner-trusted.

if_stuck.note:
1. **Registry apps appear** — Once the registry's apps appear, install them exactly like official-catalog apps.
2. **App never appears** — If a source shows in the UI but its app never appears in the App Store (even after a gateway restart), the repo has neither an `app-registry.json` index at its root NOR an `apps/<name>/app.json` monorepo layout — the scanner needs one of the two; a single `app.json` at the repo root is not discovered.
3. **Internal registry refresh fails** — On an internal deployment, a 'Could not refresh: internal' error is a git-auth failure to your forge — see the internal App Store registry entry.

entries.crew_prompt: Help me add my team's external Kiro Crew app registry. In the dashboard, open the Apps → Discover page, click the Sources gear, and add a registry with a name, the git-cloneable repo URL, and a branch. Then hit Refresh so the store re-fetches. Explain that external apps are cloned anonymously (repo must be public) unless the same-repo carve-out applies, and that a SOURCE count of 0 just means its apps are already installed.

steps.do: In the dashboard, go to Settings → Computer Use.
steps.expect: It is OFF by default — the primary enable lives in a protected file (`~/.kiro/crew/computer_use.json`) that the agent can neither read nor write, so only you (through this panel) can turn it on.

steps.do: This applies on macOS.
steps.do_zh: 适用于 macOS。
steps.expect: The panel shows Accessibility and Screen Recording rows with an 'Open System Settings' button. These probes are ADVISORY — the copy says 'Not detected does not always mean unavailable' (macOS attributes the grant to the responsible parent app), and the feature is never gated on them. Windows needs no such grant. Linux is unsupported and the panel shows the reason with no toggle.

steps.do: For example, in chat: "Rename the top file in my Documents Finder window to notes-2026.md".

entries.title: When Computer Use touches your mouse and keyboard
entries.title_zh: Computer Use 何时会动鼠标和键盘
entries.symptom: Before Crew drives your desktop, you want to know which actions move the cursor or take keyboard focus on macOS and Windows.

steps.do: Linux returns a typed refusal ("computer use is not supported on this platform") — relay it and stop, don't retry.
steps.expect: macOS and Windows both drive the FULL tool set. The difference between macOS and Windows is only HOW input is delivered, not what is supported.

steps.do_zh: 默认方式不会移动光标。
steps.expect: Addressing an element by `element_index` performs the control's own action (macOS `AXPress`, Windows UIA patterns). It moves neither your physical mouse nor your keyboard focus on EITHER platform. This is what `click_method: "auto"` picks whenever an index is present, and it is always the pointer-safe choice.
steps.t_zh: 使用光标安全默认方式

steps.do: Pass an `element_index`, or name `global` to accept the cursor move.
steps.expect: macOS can post a located click to an app WITHOUT moving your cursor (`app_post`). Windows has NO per-process input, so any coordinate click moves your real cursor and any keystroke takes your keyboard focus. Consequences on Windows: `auto` + coordinates is refused; `app_post`/`sky_click` are macOS-only and refuse by name.

steps.do: `click_method: "global"` moves your real pointer and must be NAMED by the model. A `computer_drag` on Windows must pass `click_method: "global"` explicitly (the default app-scoped route is refused there, since Windows has no pointer-free drag).
steps.expect: `auto` never resolves onto it, so the cursor is never warped by accident, and every such use is separately audited. Kiro should tell you before it takes your cursor.

entries.crew_prompt: I'm on Windows and computer use is enabled. Explain, for the task I'm about to give you, which actions will move my real mouse or take my keyboard focus and which won't — then prefer element-index actions wherever possible and warn me before any step that moves my cursor.

entries.title: Zero-token crons: run scripts or commands without an LLM
entries.title_zh: 零 token 定时：直接运行脚本或命令
entries.symptom: Your polling is deterministic, so you don't want each run to spend LLM tokens.

steps.do:
Create `~/.kiro/crew/crons/my.py`. Scripts MUST live under `~/.kiro/crew/crons/` (the path is validated). A minimal body:

from kiro_crew.cron_script import Done, Report, Skip

def run(ctx):
    result = ctx.call_tool("server-name", "tool-name", {"key": "value"})
    ctx.notify(result)
    raise Report("Result recorded; keep this cron scheduled")

Here `ctx.message` = the job's message (arguments), `ctx.notify()` delivers, `Skip()` ends the tick silently, `Done()` completes and removes the job, `Report(msg)` delivers and keeps the job.
steps.t: Put the script in the required directory

steps.expect: Runs the function with REAL MCP tools, but notifications are printed instead of delivered — so you can debug without spamming yourself.
steps.t: Preview the script before scheduling it

steps.do: In chat, ask Kiro to add a cron with script='~/.kiro/crew/crons/my.py:function' and every=300. For a one-liner instead, ask for a command cron (a shell command) — mutually exclusive with script. Note: `--script`/`--command` are not CLI flags; create these through chat/MCP or the dashboard Schedule page.
steps.expect: A script cron bypasses the LLM entirely (zero tokens).
steps.t: Register the zero-token job through chat or MCP
steps.t_zh: 通过聊天或 MCP 登记零 token 任务

entries.crew_prompt: I have a Python function at ~/.kiro/crew/crons/my.py:run that does deterministic polling. Register it as a script cron that runs every 5 minutes so it spends no LLM tokens. First preview it for me, then schedule it.

steps.do_zh: 开启设置前会拒绝。
steps.expect: These refuse until you opt in, returning a clear 422 that names the setting: script-type crons, script-type hooks, listing third-party MCP tools, Papyrus build and git, and AWS Polly voice replies. They all fail closed because there is no provable internal sandbox.
steps.t: Recognize what fails until you opt in

steps.do: Only if you accept agent subprocesses running as your own user. In %USERPROFILE%\.kiro\crew\config.json, add { "agent": { "sandbox_allow_unsandboxed_exec": true } }.
steps.do_zh: 只有当你接受“agent 子进程以你本人权限运行”时才开
steps.expect: Config is read live, no gateway restart needed; `kirocrew setup` also asks you once (default no). Note: turning it on means subprocesses can read your home, including .aws and .ssh — the same as running the command yourself in a shell.
steps.t_zh: 编辑 config.json 开启设置

steps.do: Currently, regardless of opt-in.
steps.do_zh: 开不开都一样。
steps.expect: Unavailable whether or not you opt in: command-type crons (sh -c), SSH tunnels / remote dashboard, Piper voice replies, project-level skills, Spec Builder's Duplicate, and Code Review Sage. They return a clear "not supported on Windows" instead of crashing.
steps.t: Know what is not supported on Windows
steps.t_zh: 了解 Windows 未支持功能

if_stuck.note: If a gh binary you trust is refused by Issue Radar, install it somewhere only you and the system can write (such as per-user %LOCALAPPDATA%), or open an issue with the exact refusal text.

entries.crew_prompt: On Windows, explain whether I need `sandbox_allow_unsandboxed_exec` for what I'm trying to do, what breaks without it, and what is simply unsupported on Windows. If I decide to enable it, edit %USERPROFILE%\.kiro\crew\config.json to set agent.sandbox_allow_unsandboxed_exec to true and confirm it took effect (no restart needed).

entries.title: Give your Crew a searchable knowledge library
entries.title_zh: 给你的 Crew 建一个可搜索的知识库
entries.symptom: You want Kiro Crew to remember whole documents — design docs, runbooks, wiki pages, PDFs — so it can pull the exact, cited passage on demand instead of you re-pasting them into every chat.

sources.label: modules/knowledge.md — Role & boundary / Automatic write paths (§2b)

steps.do: Put whole documents (design docs, RFCs, runbooks, wiki pages) here; put short 'always/never' preferences in memory via learn (see the memory tutorial).
steps.expect: The Knowledge Library is the durable, verbatim, CITED record — the long detail memory can only paraphrase. Memory carries the small always-on picture and is injected into every prompt; the library is pulled on demand only when you (or the Crew) search it.
steps.t: Understand what belongs here vs memory

steps.do: Open the dashboard and go to the Knowledge tab. You can register a folder source (a whole directory is watched and re-scanned as files change), upload individual files, or add a URL.
steps.do_zh: 在 dashboard 的 Knowledge tab。
steps.expect: Supported types include .md, .txt, .org, source code, and — via bundled deps — .pdf and .docx. Before you confirm a folder, the tab shows an estimated file/chunk/LLM-call count so you can see the cost, since each chunk is one extraction call.
steps.t: Add documents from dashboard Knowledge tab
steps.t_zh: 从 Knowledge 页添加文档

steps.do: Turn on `knowledge.auto_add_documents` in `~/.kiro/crew/config.json` (default false).
steps.expect: Then when the agent reads a load-bearing doc during a task, it calls its `knowledge_add_document` tool to file the TEXT into one aggregate 'Auto-added' source. Kiro Crew fetches nothing itself — the agent reads the content with its own tools under your approval, so `doc_ingest_hosts` does not apply here.
steps.t: Let Crew add documents it reads
steps.t_zh: 让 Crew 自动添加所读文档

steps.do: Turn on `knowledge.auto_register_project_docs` (default false).
steps.expect: Each project dir you work in is registered as a read-only folder source carrying a document filter: only .md/.pdf/.docx/.org above a size floor, excluding agent-instruction files (AGENTS.md), generated files, and repo boilerplate — never source code. Once on it applies to every project, with no per-project confirmation.
steps.t_zh: 开启项目文档自动登记

steps.do: Ask a question that references your docs, e.g. "what do we know about the auth token design?" You can also browse and search directly in the dashboard Knowledge tab.
steps.expect: The Crew calls its `local_knowledge_search` tool (hybrid FTS5 keyword + entity-graph + vector search fused with RRF) and answers WITH a citation back to the source file/section and line range.
steps.t_zh: 直接询问 Crew 搜索文档

if_stuck.note: If the same document shows up under two sources (e.g. a folder copy plus a one-shot upload), run a dedup pass to collapse the duplicates.

entries.crew_prompt: Help me set up my Knowledge Library so you can remember my documents. First explain the difference between what belongs in the Knowledge Library vs. in memory. Then, if I enable `knowledge.auto_add_documents` and `knowledge.auto_register_project_docs`, describe what each will ingest. Finally, run a search against the library for a topic I care about and show me the citation you get back. List my current sources with your knowledge_list_sources tool.

entries.title: Remove duplicate knowledge-library documents
entries.title_zh: 清理知识库中的重复文档
entries.symptom: The same document was picked up from two places — a folder copy and a one-shot upload, say — and you want to collapse the duplicates so search results and per-source counts stay clean.

steps.do: Use a dry-run that changes nothing. Tell your Crew: "do a dry-run dedup of my knowledge base."
steps.do_zh: 这是干跑，不改任何东西。
steps.expect: It calls its `knowledge_dedup` tool, which DEFAULTS to a dry-run preview: it lists which duplicate would be deleted and which copy is kept, without touching anything. Matching is conservative — exact extracted-text hashes collapse first; a fuzzy match needs BOTH a filename near-match AND an embedding cosine similarity of at least 0.95 in the same embedding space.
steps.t: Ask your Crew to preview duplicates
steps.t_zh: 让 Crew 预览重复项

steps.do: Only if the preview is right. Then ask for another dry-run to confirm nothing is left to collapse.
steps.do_zh: 前提是预览无误。
steps.expect: The Crew re-runs `knowledge_dedup` with apply=true. Duplicates collapse into one stored copy. A shared document is NOT destroyed — the loser's source is attached as a location of the winner, so the doc still appears under both sources without inflating the Library total.
steps.t: Apply it and confirm nothing is left
steps.t_zh: 执行合并并确认无剩余

steps.do: Add `--apply` to actually collapse them.
steps.expect: The bare command is the dry-run preview (lists what would collapse, changes nothing). Same conservative match rule as the Crew uses.
steps.t: Run the same thing in the terminal

steps.do: A full pass also runs automatically. Ask the Crew (or run the command) when you want it cleaned up now rather than on the next sweep.
steps.do_zh: 后台也会自动全量清理。
steps.expect: You do not have to run this constantly. The watcher runs a full duplicate-collapsing pass every `knowledge.dedup_every_n_sweeps` sweeps (default 12, roughly hourly; 0 disables). The per-write gate only catches byte-identical documents on ingest, so the periodic pass is what catches near-duplicates and pre-existing ones.
steps.t: Ask the Crew to run it now
steps.t_zh: 让 Crew 立即运行清理

if_stuck.note: If a source still looks wrong after dedup, review its documents in the dashboard Knowledge tab — per-source badge counts are filter-aware and show what each source actually holds.

entries.crew_prompt: Please clean up duplicate documents in my Knowledge Library. First run a dry-run preview (no changes) and show me which duplicates would be collapsed and which copy is kept. Explain the match rule you're relying on. Then, only after I confirm, apply the dedup and re-run the preview to show nothing is left.

entries.title: Connect an external tool to your Crew
entries.title_zh: 给 Crew 接入外部工具
entries.symptom: You want your Crew to use an MCP server for Slack, a database, or another API.

steps.do: In the dashboard — no config files to hand-edit. Go to Agent Capabilities → MCP Servers (the /capabilities route).
steps.do_zh: 在 dashboard 中——不用手改配置文件。
steps.expect: You see a table of MCP servers with status badges; the two built-ins (kirocrew-core and kirocrew-cron) are always there.
steps.t_zh: 打开 MCP Servers 页面

steps.do: The modal takes the exact `mcpServers` JSON you'd copy from a README. Paste a {"mcpServers": {...}} block ("command" must be the FULL path to the server binary, plus any "args"/"env"), or paste a single spec and type a Name. Tick "Enable immediately" so it turns on right away (otherwise it lands disabled).
steps.do_zh: 弹窗接收的就是你从 README 里复制的那段 `mcpServers` JSON。
steps.expect: A live preview lists the server(s) that will be added, and a warning appears if the JSON is malformed.
steps.t: Click Add Custom and paste config
steps.t_zh: 点击 Add Custom 并粘贴配置

steps.do: Freshly-started chat sessions pick up the tool. Already-open sessions keep the old tool list. Alternatively, flip the server's toggle on in the table.
steps.do_zh: 新开的会话会拿到这个工具；已经开着的会话还是旧清单。
steps.expect: The gateway restarts and your server shows up enabled in the list.

steps.do: Kiro Crew probes it with a real handshake.
steps.do_zh: Kiro Crew 会用一次真实握手去探测它。
steps.expect: A green "Online" badge appears next to your server in the MCP Servers table. (If you prefer a terminal, `kirocrew doctor` reports the same probe status.)

if_stuck.note:
1. **Global MCP install is insufficient** — Installing a server only in the global `~/.kiro/settings/mcp.json` is NOT enough — Kiro Crew agents don't read it.
2. **Agent MCP configuration required** — Edit `~/.kiro/agents/kirocrew.json`: add the server under `mcpServers` AND add `@XX` to the `tools` array, then `kirocrew restart` (MCP servers load at process start).
3. **Dashboard cannot register servers** — The dashboard MCP panel only shows status; it can't register a new server.
4. **Verify MCP setup** — Verify with `kirocrew doctor`.

entries.crew_prompt: Walk me through adding a new MCP server from the dashboard so my agent can use its tools. Open Agent Capabilities → MCP Servers, use "Add Custom" to paste this config: <CONFIG_OR_MCPSERVERS_BLOCK> (command is the FULL path to the binary), tick "Enable immediately", then Apply & Restart. Confirm the server shows a green "Online" badge and tell me the tool names it exposes.

entries.title: What your Crew can do out of the box
entries.title_zh: Crew 开箱即用的能力
entries.symptom: You want to know what your Crew can do before installing anything — scheduling, subagents, memory, messaging.

steps.do: In chat, ask: "what can you already do without me installing anything?"
steps.expect: The Crew explains its two built-in tool servers — kirocrew-cron (scheduling & reminders) and kirocrew-core (subagents, memory, messaging, artifacts, and more). These are always present; you never install them.
steps.t: Ask your Crew for the fastest tour
steps.t_zh: 让 Crew 快速介绍功能

steps.do: Just ask in chat. Ask: "what jobs do I have scheduled?" From a terminal, run `kirocrew cron list`.
steps.do_zh: 在聊天里直接问。
steps.expect: The Crew lists your scheduled jobs, or tells you there are none yet. Scheduling, pausing, and one-shot reminders all come from this built-in server. The terminal shows the same thing.
steps.t_zh: 试用 kirocrew-cron 定时能力

steps.do: Ask what it remembers about you. Ask: "what have you learned about how I like things done?" From a terminal, run `kirocrew learn list`.
steps.do_zh: 问它记住了你的哪些偏好。
steps.expect: The Crew lists the corrections and preferences it remembers across sessions, or tells you it has none yet. Memory, subagents (spawn), artifacts, and proactive messaging are all core tools with no setup.
steps.t_zh: 试用 kirocrew-core 记忆能力

steps.do: In the dashboard, where the full list is shown.
steps.do_zh: 在 dashboard 查看清单。
steps.expect: kirocrew-core and kirocrew-cron are listed with green "Online" badges — you never install them. This is the same page where you'd later add an external server.
steps.t_zh: 打开 MCP connections 清单

if_stuck.note: Want a capability that isn't built in — Slack, a database, a private API? Add it as an external MCP server

entries.crew_prompt: Give me a plain-language tour of the built-in MCP tools you already have (kirocrew-core and kirocrew-cron): what you can schedule, remember, delegate to subagents, and notify me about — without me installing anything. For each group, give me one example prompt I could send you right now.

entries.title: Decide which tools run on their own and which ask you first
entries.title_zh: 决定哪些工具自动跑、哪些先问你
entries.symptom: Your Crew asks permission for every action, or you want trusted tools to run without prompting.

steps.do: By default, your Crew asks you before every tool call. In chat, each pending action shows an approval card you can approve or reject (you can reject several at once).
steps.do_zh: 默认情况下，Crew 在每次调用工具前都会问你。聊天里每个待办动作都有一张审批卡，可以批准或拒绝（还能一次拒绝多条）。
steps.expect: When your Crew wants to run a tool, a card appears in the chat with the tool name and its inputs, waiting for your click.
steps.t_zh: 了解默认工具审批行为

steps.do: In the chat, click the approval-mode pill in the footer and pick a mode — Normal (ask every time), Reads (read-only tools run silently, writes still ask), Trust (trust this session's tools), or YOLO (auto-approve everything, confirm-gated).
steps.do_zh: 在聊天里点底部的审批模式药丸，选一个模式——Normal（每次都问）、Reads（只读工具静默跑、写操作仍然问）、Trust（信任本次会话的工具）、YOLO（全部自动批准，需二次确认）。
steps.expect: The footer pill switches to your chosen mode. In Reads mode, read/describe/list-style tools now run without a card, while write or destructive tools still show one.
steps.t: Pick Reads for the safe middle ground
steps.t_zh: 选择 Reads 作为安全折中

steps.do: On any approval card, click Trust to stop being asked for that tool/server for the rest of the session. To make specific tools trusted permanently, open Settings → MCP and add an "autoApprove" list to that server in its config (or just ask your Crew to edit it).
steps.do_zh: 在任意审批卡上点 Trust，本次会话内这个工具/服务器就不再问你。想永久免审批具体工具，去 Settings → MCP，在该服务器配置里加一个 "autoApprove" 列表（或直接让 Crew 帮你改）。
steps.expect: After Trust, that server's matching tools skip the card for this session. After adding autoApprove and restarting, the named tools skip the prompt every session. Note: on shared/enterprise machines a security policy can still force a tool it has an opinion about back through the prompt — auto-approve does not override the governance ceiling.
steps.t: Trust one server's tools going forward
steps.t_zh: 长期信任指定服务器工具

steps.do: In Settings → Security, or ask your Crew to pull the recent gated tool calls from its tamper-evident log.
steps.do_zh: 在 Settings → Security 中查看，或让 Crew 帮你从可防篡改的日志里拉出最近经过审批闸的工具调用。
steps.expect: Settings → Security shows the live posture; the CLI (or your Crew) prints the last 20 security events, including tool approvals and any auto-approve grants the policy withheld.
steps.t: Review security posture and audit surfaces
steps.t_zh: 查看安全态势和审计面

if_stuck.note:
1. **Unsure which tools are safe** — Not sure which tools are safe to auto-approve? Start by seeing what the built-in tools do
2. **Compound read commands still prompt** — The 'Reads' approval mode splits a compound command on `;` `&&` `||` `|` and evaluates each segment independently, auto-approving only a single read-only invocation — so `cd abc && grep xyz` still prompts (the `cd` segment isn't read-only).
3. **Sessions expose only builder-mcp** — If sessions only expose builder-mcp even though the dashboard shows all your MCP servers healthy, it's a known bug: add your server to the agent file's `tools` AND `allowedTools`.
4. **Agent reports wrong tool list** — Also note the agent hallucinates its own tool list when asked 'what MCPs do you have?' — trust the config, not the answer.

entries.crew_prompt: Explain how tool approval works in Kiro Crew: the default per-call approval card, the chat-footer approval-mode picker (Normal / Reads / Trust / YOLO), the per-card Trust action, and how per-server autoApprove works in my MCP config. Then help me set it up so read-only tools run without asking but anything that writes or deletes still prompts me — using the Reads mode. Afterward, show me my recent security events.

entries.title: Teach your Crew a lasting preference or correction
entries.title_zh: 让 Crew 记住偏好或纠正
entries.symptom: You keep repeating the same instruction and want Kiro Crew to remember it for good — a style, a rule, or a 'never do that again' correction.

steps.do: In any chat, say something like "Always use dark mode" or "Never use rm -rf without confirmation" or "Remember that our team uses pytest".
steps.do_zh: 在任意对话里。
steps.expect: Kiro Crew saves it right away via its learn_add tool and confirms it will remember. Phrases like 'always', 'never', and 'remember' are what trigger a save.

steps.do: Say 'remember ...' explicitly if you want it saved on the spot.
steps.expect: If you correct Kiro Crew during a normal chat without saying 'remember', it does NOT save instantly — the correction is picked up later as an implicit lesson during background consolidation (after ~3 hours idle).

steps.do: Open the dashboard and go to Overview → Memory. Prefer the terminal? `kirocrew learn list` prints the same list.
steps.expect: Your saved lessons are listed there, and the Overview page shows a Lessons count. Lessons are global (shared across all your workspaces) unless scoped to one repository.

steps.do: In Overview → Memory, delete the lesson from the list, or just tell your Crew 'forget the dark-mode rule'. Prefer the terminal? `kirocrew learn remove "dark mode"` removes any lesson whose text contains that phrase.
steps.expect: It disappears from the list immediately.
steps.t: Remove a lesson from the list

if_stuck.note:
1. **Lesson does not apply** — If a lesson does not seem to apply, open your memory to see exactly what is stored and edit it directly. Auto-injection at session start is the intended behavior; needing to ask means something is off.
2. **Memory retrieval is split** — Memory is split: semantic memory (preferences/rules/lessons) is injected at session start within a fixed budget; episodic memory (conversation fragments) is retrieved per-prompt only.
3. **Data Home is wrong** — Check `kirocrew doctor` shows Data Home `~/.kiro/crew` (not `~/.priortool`).
4. **Known learn_add write bug** — On `0.5.0.x` a known `learn_add` write bug (missing `X-Session-Key`) is fixed by `kirocrew config set mcp_gateway.forward_declared_env true` + restart.

entries.crew_prompt: I want you to permanently remember a preference. Please save this as a lesson so it applies in future sessions: <write your rule here, e.g. 'always run the frontend checks before calling a change done'>. After saving, point me to it in Overview → Memory (or run `kirocrew learn list`) so I can confirm it is stored.

entries.title: See and edit what your Crew remembers
entries.title_zh: 查看并编辑 Crew 记住的内容
entries.symptom: You want to review what Kiro Crew knows about you and your projects, then fix anything wrong.

steps.do: Open Overview → Memory. Prefer the terminal? `kirocrew memory show` (add a target like `kirocrew memory show preferences` to narrow it).
steps.expect: It shows your memory in one place: your preferences, your project context, and your daily history, plus the semantic/episodic store and lessons. The terminal prints the same three markdown layers.
steps.t: View your Crew's memory in dashboard
steps.t_zh: 在 dashboard 查看 Crew 记忆

steps.do: Ask your Crew 'search your memory for pytest'. Prefer the terminal? `kirocrew memory search "pytest"`; `kirocrew memory list`; `kirocrew memory stats`.
steps.expect: It runs the search and summarizes the hits. `kirocrew memory search "pytest"` searches BOTH stores and labels each hit (semantic/episodic recall vs keyword markdown hits); `kirocrew memory list` browses semantic entries and `kirocrew memory stats` shows counts.
steps.t: Search memory by meaning or keyword
steps.t_zh: 按含义或关键词搜索记忆

steps.do: In Overview → Memory, edit preferences.md or projects.md directly.
steps.expect: Your changes are saved as your explicit input, which outranks anything the consolidator wrote automatically.
steps.t: Edit preferences or projects in dashboard
steps.t_zh: 在 dashboard 编辑偏好或项目

steps.do: In chat, tell it to update its memory files (e.g. 'update your projects note to say we shipped v2').
steps.expect: It edits the markdown files for you. No manual file editing needed.
steps.t: Ask Kiro Crew to update memory
steps.t_zh: 让 Kiro Crew 更新记忆

if_stuck.note: To add a durable rule rather than free-form notes, save it as a lesson instead.

entries.crew_prompt: Please show me everything you currently remember about me and my projects. Open Overview → Memory (or run `kirocrew memory show` and `kirocrew memory list`), summarize what is stored in plain language, and point out anything that looks outdated or wrong so I can decide what to fix.

media.caption: Open your crew's Memory from Settings to browse semantic and episodic memory.

entries.title: Start a conversation that leaves no memory trace
entries.title_zh: 开启不写入记忆的会话
entries.symptom: You want a sensitive or throwaway conversation that is not remembered, learned from, or saved to preferences and history.

sources.label: README.md — Incognito and temporary session modes

steps.expect: Persistent (default) reads and writes memory and consolidates. Incognito reads your existing memory for context but blocks learn_add and consolidation (nothing new is learned). Temporary is the strictest: it reads NO memory and writes none — an isolated bubble.

steps.do: In the dashboard, use the ghost button on the Welcome view, or the mode icon in the chat header, to switch that session to Incognito or Temporary.
steps.expect: The header shows the active mode so you can confirm before you start typing.
steps.t_zh: 在面板开启不留痕模式

steps.do: On Slack, prefix your message with `!incognito` or `!temporary`. On Telegram, use `/incognito` or `/temporary`. You can add your question right after the modifier to mark the conversation and answer it in one message.
steps.expect: The guarantees are the same on both channels.
steps.t: Switch modes from Slack or Telegram
steps.t_zh: 从 Slack 或 Telegram 切换模式

steps.expect: All three modes still write the session JSONL file (needed for history display and resume). Incognito blocks learn_add and consolidation; Temporary additionally blocks memory READS, so no preferences, history, or lessons are injected into the prompt.
steps.t: Know what every mode still writes
steps.t_zh: 了解各模式仍写入什么

if_stuck.note: Back in a normal (Persistent) session, use memory show to confirm nothing from the private chat was learned.

entries.crew_prompt: Explain the difference between Persistent, Incognito, and Temporary memory modes in plain language, and tell me exactly how to switch this session to a no-trace mode on the dashboard, on Slack, and on Telegram. I want a conversation that is not learned from or saved into my preferences.

entries.title: Back up or migrate your Crew's memory
entries.title_zh: 备份或迁移 Crew 的记忆
entries.symptom: You want to move Kiro Crew to a new machine, back up its memory, or migrate old markdown memory into the structured store.

steps.do: Ask your Crew, or run it yourself. Tell your Crew 'export my memory to memory-backup.json' and it runs this for you.
steps.do_zh: 让 Crew 做，或自己跑。
steps.expect: It writes the vector-store collections (semantic, episodic, lessons) to the file; without -o it prints the JSON instead. This is your portable backup. There is no dashboard button for memory export — the CLI or your Crew is the way.
steps.t: Back up everything to a JSON file
steps.t_zh: 备份全部记忆到 JSON 文件

steps.do: If you want prefs/projects/history too.
steps.do_zh: 想连偏好/项目/历史一起带上就加这个开关
steps.expect: Adds a `markdown` collection (preferences, projects, and per-day history) to the export. Without the flag the export shape is unchanged.

steps.do: Again, ask your Crew or run it.
steps.do_zh: 同样可以让 Crew 做或自己跑。
steps.expect: It restores from the JSON export with full validation. Your existing memories win on conflict and re-importing the same item is idempotent, so it is safe to run more than once.
steps.t: Restore it on the new machine

steps.do: Rarely needed.
steps.do_zh: 通常不用手动做。
steps.expect: One-time migration: preferences.md → semantic entries, history/*.md → episodic entries. Migration is automatic in the background at gateway startup, so this manual command is only an escape hatch; it is idempotent and skips entries that already exist.
steps.t: Fold legacy markdown into the structured store
steps.t_zh: 转换旧 markdown 到结构化存储

if_stuck.note: After importing or migrating, run memory show and memory stats to confirm your entries are present.

entries.crew_prompt: I want to back up my Kiro Crew memory and move it to another machine. Please run `kirocrew memory export --include-markdown -o memory-backup.json`, explain what is in the file, and tell me the exact `kirocrew memory import` command to run on the new machine to restore it.

entries.title: Chat with your Crew in Microsoft Teams
entries.title_zh: 在 Microsoft Teams 中与 Crew 聊天
entries.symptom: You want to DM your Kiro Crew agent in a Teams 1:1 chat — but Teams is the one channel that needs a public HTTPS webhook, not just a token.
entries.version_note: Internal edition is Slack-only: the enterprise policy layer permits the Slack channel and denies the rest, so this guide applies to the public build only.

steps.do: Unlike every other channel, Teams uses the Bot Framework, which PUSHES messages to a webhook. Your gateway must be reachable at a public HTTPS URL.
steps.do_zh: 与其它渠道不同，Teams 用 Bot Framework 把消息推送到 webhook，你的网关必须有一个公网 HTTPS URL。
steps.expect: You have (or will set up) one of: a reverse proxy terminating TLS in front of the gateway, a public-hostname VM/App Service, or a dev tunnel for testing (devtunnel host -p 5476 or ngrok http 5476). Teams will NOT deliver to a plain-HTTP or SSH-tunneled endpoint.
steps.t_zh: 了解 Teams 特殊要求

steps.do: So the gateway can validate inbound Bot Framework JWTs (or ask your Crew to run it). If you cloned the repo, `pip install -e ".[teams]"` also works.
steps.do_zh: 让网关能校验入站的 Bot Framework JWT（或让 Crew 帮你跑）
steps.expect: pyjwt and cryptography install. Without the extra the channel is skipped with an actionable log line, and the Settings → Channels → Teams panel shows a 'PyJWT required' notice.

steps.do: In the Azure Portal. Note its Microsoft App ID (Client ID), create a client secret (the App Password), and for a single-tenant bot note the Tenant ID. Under the bot's Channels, add the Microsoft Teams channel.
steps.do_zh: 在 Azure Portal。记下它的 Microsoft App ID（Client ID），创建一个 client secret（即 App Password），单租户机器人还要记下 Tenant ID。
steps.expect: You have an App ID and a client secret value.
steps.t_zh: 创建 Azure Bot 资源

steps.do: To your public URL plus the Kiro Crew route
steps.do_zh: 你的公网 URL 加上 Kiro Crew 的路由
steps.expect: The endpoint reads https://<your-public-host>/api/messaging/teams

steps.do: Settings → Channels → Teams. Paste your credentials: App (client) ID, App password (client secret), and Tenant ID (only for a single-tenant bot). The panel stores the secret in your .env for you — it is never written to config.json.
steps.do_zh: Settings → Channels → Teams。粘贴凭证：App（client）ID、App password（client secret）、Tenant ID（仅单租户机器人需要）。面板会把密钥替你写进 .env，绝不写进 config.json。
steps.expect: The three credential fields show as set; the App password field shows a masked '••••••' once stored.
steps.t_zh: 打开 Teams 渠道设置

steps.do: In the same panel, the controls are Enable Teams channel and the allowed users list (your email/UPN or AAD object id). An empty allow-list denies everyone (fail closed). Then click Save Teams settings.
steps.do_zh: 在同一面板；控件为 Enable Teams channel 和 allowed users（邮箱/UPN 或 AAD object id）。空名单=谁都拒（fail closed）。然后点 Save Teams settings。
steps.expect: The panel shows Saved and asks you to restart to apply. Teams reliably carries the sender's AAD object id, so listing object ids also works when email is absent.
steps.t: Enable Teams channel and add yourself
steps.t_zh: 启用 Teams 并添加自己

expect.default: On a desktop app, quit and reopen it (the gateway restarts with the app); on a CLI/Linux gateway run the command, or just ask your Crew to restart. The Settings → Channels → Teams badge turns Active/green once the outbound app credentials validate.
expect.macos: Quit and reopen the desktop app (the gateway restarts with the app). The Settings → Channels → Teams badge turns Active/green once the outbound app credentials validate.
expect.linux: Run the command (or just ask your Crew to restart). The Settings → Channels → Teams badge turns Active/green once the outbound app credentials validate.
expect.cloud-desktop: Run the command (or just ask your Crew to restart). The Settings → Channels → Teams badge turns Active/green once the outbound app credentials validate.

steps.do: Reference your App ID (Teams Developer Portal → Apps → New app → add a Bot with your App ID, scope Personal), set supportsFiles to true, side-load it (Apps → Manage your apps → Upload a custom app), then open a 1:1 chat with the bot and send a message; so you must use a 1:1 personal chat.
steps.do_zh: 引用你 App ID（Teams Developer Portal → Apps → New app → 加一个用你 App ID 的 Bot，scope 选 Personal），把 supportsFiles 设为 true，侧载它（Apps → Manage your apps → Upload a custom app），然后和机器人开一对一私聊并发消息。
steps.expect: The bot replies in your personal chat. Messages in team channels or group chats are refused (fail closed).
steps.t_zh: 打包 Teams 应用清单

if_stuck.note: No reply usually means: the webhook isn't public HTTPS, your email/object id isn't in the allowed users list on the Teams panel, or the kirocrew[teams] extra isn't installed (the panel shows a 'PyJWT required' notice).

entries.crew_prompt: Help me connect Kiro Crew to Microsoft Teams as a DM-only bot. Walk me through: installing the kirocrew[teams] extra, creating an Azure Bot with an App ID and client secret and adding the Teams channel, exposing my gateway at a public HTTPS URL and setting the bot's messaging endpoint to https://<host>/api/messaging/teams, then entering the App ID / client secret / Tenant ID and my email in Settings → Channels → Teams, enabling the channel and saving, restarting the gateway, and side-loading a personal-scope Teams app manifest. Confirm the Settings → Channels → Teams badge turns Active.

entries.title: Chat with your Crew in Cisco Webex
entries.title_zh: 在 Cisco Webex 中与 Crew 聊天
entries.symptom: You want to chat with your agent from Webex using only a bot token, with no public URL or webhook.
entries.version_note: Internal edition is Slack-only: the enterprise policy layer permits the Slack channel and denies the rest, so this guide applies to the public build only.

steps.do: It needs NO public URL and NO webhook. Kiro Crew registers a device and receives messages over an outbound WebSocket, so it works from behind a firewall or NAT. You need a running gateway and a Webex account.
steps.do_zh: 无需公网 URL、无需 webhook，走出站 WebSocket，防火墙/NAT 后也能用。你只需一个在跑的网关和一个 Webex 账号。
steps.expect: Your gateway is running and you can log in at developer.webex.com.
steps.t_zh: 了解 Webex 出站连接优势

steps.do: At developer.webex.com, open My Webex Apps → Create a New App → Create a Bot, fill in name/username/icon, and copy the Bot access token (shown only once; regenerate later from the app's edit page if lost).
steps.do_zh: 在 developer.webex.com 打开 My Webex Apps → Create a New App → Create a Bot，填名字/用户名/图标，复制 Bot access token（只显示一次；丢了可在应用编辑页重新生成）。
steps.expect: You have a Bot access token string.
steps.t: Create a bot in My Webex Apps
steps.t_zh: 在 Webex 创建机器人

steps.do: The Bot access token field is under Settings → Channels → Webex. The panel stores it in your .env for you (kept out of config.json).
steps.do_zh: Bot access token 的 token 栏位于 Settings → Channels → Webex。面板会替你存进 .env（不落进 config.json）。
steps.expect: The token field shows as set (masked). On save the panel verifies the token with Webex.

steps.do: The controls are Enable Webex channel and the allowed emails list, which must include your own Webex email (an empty list rejects everyone). Then click Save Webex settings.
steps.do_zh: 控件名为 Enable Webex channel；allowed emails 需包含自己的 Webex 邮箱（空名单=全部拒绝）。然后点 Save Webex settings。
steps.expect: The panel shows Saved — and 'Verified with Webex' when the token checks out — and asks you to restart to apply.
steps.t: Enable Webex and add allowed email
steps.t_zh: 启用 Webex 并添加邮箱

steps.do: In Webex, search for your bot's username; Desktop app: quit and reopen; CLI/Linux: run the command (or ask your Crew to restart).
steps.do_zh: 在 Webex 里按用户名找到机器人。

expect.default: The Settings → Channels → Webex badge turns Active and the bot replies to your DM. No reply usually means your email isn't in the allowed list; a badge stuck on Needs setup means the token isn't set or is invalid.
expect.macos: The Settings → Channels → Webex badge turns Active and the bot replies to your DM. No reply usually means your email isn't in the allowed list; a badge stuck on Needs setup means the token isn't set or is invalid.
expect.linux: The Settings → Channels → Webex badge turns Active and the bot replies to your DM. No reply usually means your email isn't in the allowed list; a badge stuck on Needs setup means the token isn't set or is invalid.
expect.cloud-desktop: The Settings → Channels → Webex badge turns Active and the bot replies to your DM. No reply usually means your email isn't in the allowed list; a badge stuck on Needs setup means the token isn't set or is invalid.

steps.t: Restart the gateway and message bot
steps.t_zh: 重启网关并私信机器人

if_stuck.note: Group spaces are off by default and must be enabled separately (Allow group spaces + a room-id allow-list on the panel), with the bot @-mentioned on every message; DMs need none of this.

entries.crew_prompt: Help me connect Kiro Crew to Cisco Webex. Walk me through creating a bot at developer.webex.com and copying its Bot access token, pasting it into Settings → Channels → Webex, enabling the channel with my email in the allowed emails list, saving, and restarting the gateway. Then have me DM the bot and confirm the Settings → Channels → Webex badge turns Active.

entries.title: Chat with your Crew in WeCom
entries.title_zh: 在企业微信（WeCom）中与 Crew 聊天
entries.symptom: You want to message your agent through a WeCom AI bot with no callback URL or open port.
entries.version_note: Internal edition is Slack-only: the enterprise policy layer permits the Slack channel and denies the rest, so this guide applies to the public build only.

steps.do: This connects through WeCom, the work edition of WeChat, via its AI-bot API — NOT a personal WeChat account. Like Telegram it is outbound-only (a secure WebSocket), so there is no callback URL or open port to manage. You need a running gateway and admin access to your WeCom console.
steps.do_zh: 这是连企业微信（WeCom）的 AI 机器人，不是个人微信；出站 WebSocket，无需回调 URL 或开放端口。你需要一个在跑的网关和企业微信管理台的管理权限。
steps.expect: You have a running gateway and can open the WeCom admin console.
steps.t_zh: 明确 WeCom 连接范围

steps.do: In the WeCom admin console open Apps -> AI Agents. Its settings page shows a Bot ID and a Secret.
steps.do_zh: 在企业微信管理台打开 应用 -> AI 智能体。它的设置页会显示一个 Bot ID 和一个 Secret。
steps.expect: You have a Bot ID and a Secret. These two values are all Kiro Crew needs — no corp ID, agent ID, callback URL, or AES key.
steps.t_zh: 创建 WeCom AI 机器人

steps.do: Every WeCom member has a userid.
steps.do_zh: 每个企业微信成员都有一个 userid。
steps.expect: You have at least your own userid.

steps.do: Paste the Bot ID and the Secret into their fields. The panel stores the secret in your .env for you.
steps.do_zh: 把 Bot ID 和 Secret 分别粘进对应栏。面板会替你把密钥写进 .env。
steps.expect: Both the Bot ID and Secret fields show as set (the Secret masked).
steps.t_zh: 打开 WeCom 渠道设置

steps.do: An empty list = owner only. Then click Save.
steps.do_zh: 空名单=仅本人。然后点保存。
steps.expect: The panel shows Saved; the status badge tracks the gateway and turns connected after a restart.
steps.t: Turn on WeCom and add your userid
steps.t_zh: 开启 WeCom 并添加 userid

steps.do: Desktop app: quit and reopen; CLI/Linux: run the command (or ask your Crew to restart).

expect.default: The Settings → Channels → WeCom badge turns connected and the bot answers.
expect.macos: The Settings → Channels → WeCom badge turns connected and the bot answers.
expect.linux: The Settings → Channels → WeCom badge turns connected and the bot answers.
expect.cloud-desktop: The Settings → Channels → WeCom badge turns connected and the bot answers.

steps.t: Restart the gateway and message the bot
steps.t_zh: 重启网关并给机器人发消息

if_stuck.note: DM only: messaging the bot in a WeCom group is refused and logged. Buttons don't render, so options appear as a numbered list — reply with the number to choose.

entries.crew_prompt: Help me connect Kiro Crew to WeCom via a WeCom AI bot. Walk me through creating an AI bot under Apps -> AI Agents and copying its Bot ID and Secret, entering them in Settings → Channels → WeCom, enabling the channel with my userid in the allow-list, saving, and restarting the gateway. Then have me DM the bot and confirm the Settings → Channels → WeCom badge turns connected.

entries.title: Talk to your Crew from personal WeChat
entries.title_zh: 从个人微信 (微信) 和你的 Crew 聊天
entries.symptom: You want to chat with your agent from a personal WeChat account via the iLink bot API — a QR scan, HTTP long-poll, no public endpoint. (Unofficial surface; read the risks.)
entries.version_note: Internal edition is Slack-only: the enterprise policy layer permits the Slack channel and denies the rest, so this guide applies to the public build only.

steps.do: This connects PERSONAL WeChat through Tencent's unofficial iLink bot API. Behaviour can change without notice, using a personal account as a bot may violate WeChat's ToS, and accounts can be limited or banned. For anything business-critical use the WeCom channel instead. It is DM-only (iLink bot identities do not receive group events) and only one gateway may poll a given credential at a time.
steps.do_zh: 这是个人微信的非官方 iLink 接口，可能违反微信 ToS、账号有被限制风险；业务关键场景请改用 WeCom。仅私聊。
steps.expect: You accept the risk and are not linking a business-critical account. No public endpoint, webhook, or tunnel is required.

steps.do: In the dashboard, turn on the "Enable the WeChat channel" switch.
steps.do_zh: 在仪表盘中，打开「Enable the WeChat channel」开关。
steps.expect: The WeChat panel opens with a status pill (it reads "Not signed in" until you connect) and the enable switch flips on. Nothing is written to a file by hand — the panel saves for you.
steps.t_zh: 打开 WeChat 频道设置

steps.do: On the same panel, scan the code with the WeChat mobile app, and confirm on your phone.
steps.do_zh: 在同一面板，用手机微信 App 扫码并在手机上确认。
steps.expect: A QR appears in the panel and the app polls the scan status. After you confirm on your phone the panel shows "Signed in — restart the gateway to start receiving". The bot credential is stored server-side; only the non-secret account id is shown.

steps.do: This lets it pick up the new credential, which is read once at boot. Or just tell your Crew to restart the gateway for you.
steps.do_zh: 凭据只在启动时读取一次。也可以直接让 Crew 帮你重启。
steps.expect: After the restart the status pill turns Connected.

steps.do: From the panel, the "Who can message the bot" dropdown offers "Anyone who messages the bot", "Only allowed user IDs", or "Nobody — ignore all messages". Then add your WeChat id under the "Allowed user IDs" list that appears. (To find an id, have the person DM the bot once and read it from the gateway log.) Once your id is in the list, DM the bot.
steps.do_zh: 在面板里设置谁能私信 bot：「Who can message the bot」下拉选「Only allowed user IDs」；出现「Allowed user IDs」列表后，把你的微信 id 填进去。无需手改 config.json。
steps.expect: The dropdown defaults to "Only allowed user IDs" with an EMPTY list, which authorizes nobody (fail-closed). The bot answers once your id is in the list. Everything saves in place — no config.json editing.

if_stuck.note:
1. **Expired iLink session** — `errcode -14` = expired session, click Connect via QR again to rescan.
2. **iLink rate limit** — `errcode -2` = iLink rate limit, the poller backs off automatically.
3. **aiohttp missing at startup** — If startup reports `aiohttp` missing, install the messaging extra.
4. **Group messages are ignored** — Group messages being ignored is expected.
5. **Stuck on restart-to-connect** — If it stays on "Signed in — restart to connect", restart once more.

entries.crew_prompt: Help me connect Kiro Crew to my personal WeChat via the iLink bot API. First explain the risks (unofficial surface, possible ToS violation and account bans, DM-only) and that WeCom is safer for business use. Then walk me through the UI: Settings → Channels → WeChat, turn on "Enable the WeChat channel", click "Connect via QR" and scan with the WeChat mobile app, restart the gateway until the pill shows Connected, then set the "Who can message the bot" dropdown to "Only allowed user IDs" and add my id to the "Allowed user IDs" list. Have me DM the bot to confirm.

entries.title: Chat with your Crew in WhatsApp
entries.title_zh: 在 WhatsApp 中与 Crew 聊天
entries.symptom: You want the agent on WhatsApp from YOUR own number — scan a QR once and the gateway joins as a linked device, like WhatsApp Web. (Unofficial protocol; read the risks.)
entries.version_note: Internal edition is Slack-only: the enterprise policy layer permits the Slack channel and denies the rest, so this guide applies to the public build only.

steps.do: This uses the unofficial WhatsApp Web protocol (neonize/whatsmeow). There is no bot account and no Meta Business API — messages come from YOUR number. Automating a personal account violates WhatsApp's ToS and numbers can be banned for abusive automation; do not link a number you cannot afford to lose. The channel ships no bulk-send affordances.
steps.do_zh: 走非官方 WhatsApp Web 协议，消息来自你自己的号码；自动化个人账号违反 WhatsApp ToS，号码可能被封，别用输不起的号。
steps.expect: You accept the risk. This links your own account as a device, not a separate bot.

steps.do: A Python dependency with no dashboard equivalent — or ask your Crew to install it for you.
steps.do_zh: 这是 Python 依赖，没有 UI 等价物——也可以让 Crew 帮你装。
steps.expect: The extra installs. `kirocrew doctor` → WhatsApp Integration section reports whether the extra is installed (a missing extra is a hard failure).
steps.t_zh: 安装 WhatsApp 扩展依赖

steps.do: In the dashboard at Settings → Channels → WhatsApp, using the "Enable the WhatsApp channel" switch. Pairing only begins once the channel is running.
steps.do_zh: 位置在仪表盘的 Settings → Channels → WhatsApp，开关名为「Enable the WhatsApp channel」；配对只有在通道运行后才开始。也可以让 Crew 帮你重启。
steps.expect: The panel's enable switch flips on and, after the restart, the "Pair with WhatsApp" card becomes active. No config.json editing needed — the toggle saves for you.
steps.t: Enable the WhatsApp channel and restart the gateway
steps.t_zh: 启用 WhatsApp 通道并重启网关

steps.do: The "Show pairing code" button is on the WhatsApp panel. On your phone, go to WhatsApp → Settings → Linked devices → Link a device; the code is the one shown in the panel.
steps.do_zh: 「Show pairing code」按钮在 WhatsApp 面板；手机上的路径是 WhatsApp → 设置 → 已连接的设备 → 连接设备，使用面板里的码。
steps.expect: The code rotates every ~20 seconds and the panel follows it until the scan lands. The status badge flips to Connected. Pairing persists in the gateway's session store, so you scan once, not per restart.
steps.t: Show pairing code and scan the code

steps.do: The self-chat serves as your command line. The "Who can message the bot" dropdown defaults to "Only me", so no allow-list edit is needed to start; widen it there (Me + allowed numbers / Anyone) only if you want to. Groups are opt-in via the Groups list on the same panel.
steps.do_zh: 自聊就是命令行。面板「Who can message the bot」默认「Only me」，无需改动即可开始；需要放宽再在那里选。群聊在同一面板的 Groups 列表里逐个开启。
steps.expect: The agent answers there with your full session context. Groups stay opt-in and are ignored until you add them in the panel.

if_stuck.note:
1. **Phone revoked the link** — A "The link was revoked" badge means the phone unlinked it — restart the gateway and use Show pairing code again.
2. **Paired but not connected** — When it says "Paired, but not connected", the reason is printed verbatim below the badge.
3. **Required extra is missing** — A missing extra makes `kirocrew doctor` report a hard failure.
4. **Revoke the linked device** — Use the panel's "Unlink this device" button to revoke the linked device.

entries.crew_prompt: Help me connect Kiro Crew to WhatsApp as a linked device on my own number. First explain the risks (unofficial WhatsApp Web protocol, ToS violation, possible bans — don't link a number I can't lose). Then walk me through installing the kirocrew[whatsapp] extra, then the UI: Settings → Channels → WhatsApp, turn on "Enable the WhatsApp channel", restart the gateway, click "Show pairing code", and scan it from my phone's Linked devices. Then have me message myself in the self-chat. Confirm with `kirocrew doctor`.

entries.title: Keep your Crew running on a spare computer
entries.title_zh: 把 Kiro Crew 装在一台常开的电脑上，一直帮你干活
entries.symptom: You want chat, scheduled jobs, and tasks to keep working after you close your laptop.

sources.label: Official guide · Remote Hosts and Mobile Access

steps.do: On the always-on machine (Debian / Ubuntu shown).
steps.do_zh: 以 Debian / Ubuntu 为例。
steps.cmd: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y git tmux python3 python3-pip python3-venv
steps.expect: The install finishes without an error; each package ends up either newly installed or already at its newest version.
steps.t: Install the basics on the machine
steps.t_zh: 在常开机器安装基础工具

steps.do: Kiro Crew talks to the model through kiro-cli.
steps.do_zh: Kiro Crew 通过 kiro-cli 与模型对话。
steps.expect: You are taken through the login flow and it ends by confirming you are signed in. There is no separate model API key to enter.
steps.t: Sign the AI agent backend in
steps.t_zh: 登录 AI 代理后端

steps.do: Build its dashboard.
steps.do_zh: 构建它的仪表盘。
steps.cmd: git clone https://github.com/kirodotdev/KiroCrew.git kirocrew && cd kirocrew && cd website && npm install && npm run build && cd .. && cp -R website/dist src/kiro_crew/static/dist && pip install .
steps.expect: The repository downloads, the dashboard bundle builds, and pip finishes with a line reporting kiro-crew was installed.
steps.t: Download, build, then install Kiro Crew
steps.t_zh: 下载构建并安装 Kiro Crew

steps.do: Everything should be healthy.
steps.do_zh: 一切应正常。
steps.expect: setup writes your configuration; doctor prints a list of checks and reports kiro-cli and Node.js as OK (it warns if Node is older than 22).
steps.t: Set it up and check everything

steps.do: It survives you disconnecting. Press Ctrl+B then D to leave it running in the background; reattach later with `tmux attach -t kirocrew`.
steps.do_zh: 这样你断开连接它也不会停。
steps.expect: The gateway starts up and keeps printing log lines.
steps.t: Do a first test run inside tmux
steps.t_zh: 在 tmux 中完成首次试跑

if_stuck.note: Once the test run works, turn it into a real service so it restarts on crash and on reboot

entries.crew_prompt: I want to run Kiro Crew 24/7 on this always-on Linux host so my chat bot, cron jobs, and task runner keep working while my laptop is off. Please install the prerequisites, clone and build Kiro Crew, install it with pip, run `kirocrew setup` and `kirocrew doctor`, and do a first gateway smoke test inside a tmux session. Tell me if anything fails.

entries.title: Open the dashboard on your laptop over SSH
entries.title_zh: 在笔记本上通过 SSH 隧道打开远程仪表盘
entries.symptom: Kiro Crew runs on another machine, and you want its dashboard in your laptop browser.

sources.label: Official guide · Reach it from a laptop or phone

steps.do: Leave this window open. Replace user@your-host.example.com with your own login and host.
steps.expect: You get a normal shell on the remote host. The tunnel lives as long as this connection does.
steps.t: Forward the dashboard port over SSH
steps.t_zh: 通过 SSH 转发 dashboard 端口

steps.do: On Linux use `xdg-open` instead of `open`; on Windows just type the address into the browser instead of running `open`; on a remote Linux host use `xdg-open`.
steps.t: Open the dashboard in your laptop browser
steps.t_zh: 在笔记本浏览器打开 dashboard

steps.do: Open its localhost URL. Open the one containing `localhost:5476` in your laptop browser — that is the one that travels through the tunnel.
steps.do_zh: 打开其中的 localhost 地址
steps.expect: It prints one or more URLs, and you land in a signed-in dashboard.
steps.t: Mint a sign-in link on the remote host
steps.t_zh: 在远程主机生成登录链接

if_stuck.note:
1. **Phones need a named tunnel** — A phone cannot use SSH port forwarding; use a named HTTPS tunnel (see the phone / remote-access tutorial).
2. **Tunnel reports connection refused** — If the SSH tunnel intermittently reports 'channel N: open failed: connect failed: Connection refused' and everything stalls, the remote gateway is not staying up: make sure it runs as a background service (see 'keep your crew alive after you log out') and is actually listening on port `5476` on the remote host, and that your `ssh -L` session has not dropped. Re-open the forward if the connection died.
3. **Dashboard asks for a token** — If it asks for a token, get one in the next step.

entries.crew_prompt: Kiro Crew is running on a remote host and I want to open its dashboard from my laptop browser. Walk me through opening an SSH tunnel that forwards port 5476, then getting a sign-in link with `kirocrew token` and opening the localhost URL. If the connection is refused, help me confirm the gateway is actually listening on the remote host.

entries.title: Use Kiro Crew from your phone
entries.title_zh: 在手机上使用 Kiro Crew
entries.symptom: You want to open the dashboard and chat from a phone, which cannot use an SSH tunnel.

sources.label: Official guide · Named HTTPS tunnel (phone) + Install as an app

steps.do: On the gateway dashboard: Settings → Overview → "Use Kiro Crew on your phone". Once Tailscale is installed and signed in, it handles the gateway steps in one click: trust the tailnet origin, publish over HTTPS with Tailscale Serve, and restart.
steps.do_zh: 网关仪表盘中的 Settings → Overview →「Use Kiro Crew on your phone」。装好并登录 Tailscale 后，它会一键完成网关设置：信任 tailnet 来源、用 Tailscale Serve 发布 HTTPS，并重启。
steps.expect: The card advances through its steps (install / sign in / MagicDNS / HTTPS, then the one-click publish) until it reaches the "On" / ready state and shows a tailnet HTTPS address. This is tailnet-only — safer than exposing the dashboard on the public internet.
steps.t: Open Settings Overview and follow the phone card
steps.t_zh: 打开 Settings Overview 并按卡片操作

steps.do: When the card is ready; alternatively, open "Connect your phone" from the sidebar.
steps.do_zh: 卡片就绪后即可；也可从侧边栏打开「Connect your phone」。
steps.expect: The QR carries a live sign-in token minted only when you click. Scanning it opens a signed-in dashboard on your phone and the link expires in a few minutes — no command typed, no token pasted.
steps.t: Show its QR code and scan it
steps.t_zh: 显示二维码并用手机扫描

steps.do: Optional, as an app (iOS Safari shown). In Safari, tap Share then "Add to Home Screen", and launch from the new icon.
steps.do_zh: 可选，作为 App；这里以 iOS Safari 为例。
steps.expect: It opens without the browser address bar. A secure HTTPS address (your tunnel) is all it requires.
steps.t: Install it to your home screen

steps.do: For a public tunnel, use a named endpoint (cloudflared shown), set dashboard.url, and restart—or ask your Crew to do it. Then use /kirocrew dashboard in a chat DM for a sign-in link. Tap the /kirocrew dashboard link within 5 minutes.

entries.title: Decide when Kiro Crew asks before it acts
entries.title_zh: 决定 Kiro Crew 动手前要不要先问你
entries.symptom: You want to control whether Kiro Crew asks before running tools or approves some or all of them automatically.

sources.label: README.md — Security and control (Defense in depth)

steps.do: The default is ask every time
steps.do_zh: 即「每次都询问」
steps.expect: Out of the box Kiro Crew runs in 'Normal' (interactive) approval: before it runs any tool or command it pauses and shows you what it wants to do, and waits for your click. Nothing runs behind your back — this is the safest setting and you do not need to change anything to get it.

steps.do: On an approval card. Start narrow
steps.do_zh: 在审批卡片上
steps.expect: The approval card in the dashboard gives four choices that get wider: approve just this exact command; approve this kind of command (e.g. any 'ls ...'); approve all read-only commands for this chat; or approve every tool for this chat. A wider 'yes' only lasts for the current chat slot, and it can never approve something the safety rules already block.
steps.t: Choose how broad this yes should be

steps.do: From the approval-mode dropdown in the chat composer footer (Normal / Reads / Trust / YOLO).
steps.do_zh: 入口在聊天输入框底部的审批模式下拉（Normal / Reads / Trust / YOLO）。
steps.expect: The picker switches this chat to auto-approving read-only actions (listing files, reading logs) while still stopping to ask before anything that changes files, runs shell commands, or touches the outside world. A good middle ground for everyday use. (The setting is per chat slot.)
steps.t_zh: 选择 Reads 减少提示

steps.do: Select it from the same dropdown and confirm, or use the owner-only /kirocrew yolo command in Slack. Set its duration in Settings → Security → YOLO / Auto-approve. Use it for throwaway/sandboxed setups, not your main machine. Headless/service installs can also set the mode at launch with `kirocrew gateway --approval reads|yolo`
steps.do_zh: 在同一下拉中选择并确认，或在 Slack 使用仅限所有者的 /kirocrew yolo。持续时长在 Settings → Security → YOLO / Auto-approve 中设置。
steps.expect: YOLO auto-approves EVERY tool with no prompts. The dropdown asks you to confirm first, Kiro Crew requires an isolated KIROCREW_HOME before allowing it, it is time-bounded (default 6 hours, up to 24h, or until-shutdown (in-memory only, cleared when the gateway restarts)), and every activation is written to the security log.
steps.t: Choose YOLO only with understood risk
steps.t_zh: 仅在了解风险时选择 YOLO

if_stuck.note:
1. **Audit approvals and denials** — Not sure what got approved and run? The security event log records every approval and denial — read it next.
2. **Set the global default** — Set a global default with `kirocrew config set agent.approval_mode auto` (config enum is auto | interactive; default auto), then restart — every new session (CLI, Slack, dashboard, cron) inherits it.
3. **Override the current session** — The in-chat Normal/Reads/Trust/YOLO switch is a live per-session override.
4. **Auto is not YOLO** — `auto` is NOT YOLO: auto runs a safety classifier that auto-approves what it judges safe and still asks on risky actions; YOLO (dangerously_skip_permissions) never asks.
5. **Security gates still apply** — Either way, some MCP tool calls stay gated at the security layer ('auto-approve withheld by security policy'), which YOLO does not override.
6. **Reads mode still prompts** — Also, in Reads mode a compound command like `cd abc && grep xyz` still prompts, because the classifier evaluates each segment and `cd` is not in the read-only verb set — drop the cd and pass the path (`grep -r xyz abc/`).

entries.crew_prompt: Explain Kiro Crew's approval modes to me in plain language: what 'Normal' (interactive, the default), 'Reads', 'Trust', and 'YOLO' each do, where to switch them (the approval-mode dropdown in the chat composer footer), and what the four approval buttons (this command / this command type / all reads / all tools) mean when a card pops up. Then tell me which mode you'd recommend for a normal work laptop and why, but do NOT change my setting without asking.

entries.title: Keep the sandbox on (and know when to turn it off)
entries.title_zh: 保持沙箱开启（以及什么时候该关掉它）
entries.symptom: You want to understand the OS sandbox that hides credentials, or SSH keys and ssh-agent stop working inside it.

sources.label: README.md — Security and control (Defense in depth)

steps.expect: On macOS and Linux, Kiro Crew wraps the AI engine so it cannot read your credential folders (like ~/.aws and ~/.ssh) even if a web page or file tries to trick it into doing so. Settings → Security → Live Security Posture lists it as an active layer ("Process sandbox"). It is one of several layers, but it is the only optional one — so it is on by default.

steps.do: The dashboard has no toggle for it. You can also ask your Crew to check.
steps.do_zh: 仪表盘没有这个开关。也可以让 Crew 代查。
steps.expect: It prints one of exactly two values: 'auto' (the default — the sandbox is on) or 'off'. If you never touched it, expect 'auto'. Windows has no Kiro Crew sandbox wrapper, so this setting is about macOS and Linux.

steps.do: Unless a specific tool breaks.
steps.do_zh: 除非某个具体工具被挡住
steps.expect: The main real-world reason to turn it off is SSH: inside the sandbox, ssh-agent forwarding (SSH_AUTH_SOCK) is switched off, so passphrase-protected keys or hardware tokens will not work. If your git-over-SSH or ssh commands fail only when run through Kiro Crew, the sandbox is the likely cause.

steps.do: Set it back with `kirocrew config set agent.sandbox auto`. Restart the gateway for the change to take effect.
steps.expect: Setting it to 'off' skips Kiro Crew's own credential-hiding wrap (on macOS it still hands isolation to the AI engine's built-in sandbox where available). The other safety layers — the file-path block, the command block, and output redaction — stay on regardless, so your keys are still defended, just with one fewer layer.

if_stuck.note: If something still cannot reach a path you expected, the security log will show you exactly what was blocked and why.

entries.crew_prompt: Tell me whether my OS sandbox is on by checking `agent.sandbox` (via `kirocrew config get agent.sandbox`) and reading it back to me. Explain in plain language what the sandbox protects, that Settings → Security shows it as an active layer, and what changes if I set it to 'off' — especially around SSH keys and ssh-agent. Note there is no dashboard toggle for this setting. Do NOT change it unless I explicitly tell you to.

entries.title: See what Kiro Crew allowed, blocked, and approved
entries.title_zh: 查看 Kiro Crew 放行、拦截和批准了什么
entries.symptom: You want a record of approvals, denied commands, and blocked credential reads—or proof that the log was not altered.

sources.label: README.md — Security and control (Defense in depth)

steps.expect: It prints the last 20 entries from the security event log — things like a tool approval, an auto-approve (YOLO) turning on or off, a denied command, or a blocked read of a credential path. Each line tells you what happened, not just that something did.
steps.t: List the most recent security events

steps.do: Raise the number as needed. This is your go-to when you are asking 'wait, what did it just do?' after an unattended or automated run.
steps.expect: Shows the last 50 entries instead of 20.
steps.t: Look further back when you need more

steps.expect: Lists the active deny rules — the categories of command Kiro Crew refuses outright (for example destructive data operations, credential exfiltration, or pushing to a protected branch). These run before any approval, so even a broad 'yes' cannot get past them.

steps.do: For a scan of past conversations for suspicious tool use, run `kirocrew security audit` instead.
steps.expect: The event log is cryptographically chained, so tampering is detectable. This command reports whether the chain is intact. A pass means the history you just read is trustworthy.
steps.t: Confirm the log has not been altered

if_stuck.note: If you see approvals you did not expect, revisit your approval mode — you may be running wider than you intended.

entries.crew_prompt: Run `kirocrew security events` and read the recent security events back to me in plain language — point out any denied commands or auto-approve (YOLO) activations. Then run `kirocrew security verify` and tell me whether the log's integrity check passed. Explain what each event means; do not take any action to change my security settings.

entries.title: Skills: reusable instructions loaded on demand
entries.title_zh: Skills：随需加载的可复用操作手册
entries.symptom: You want to know what a Skill is, where to find yours, and how it enters a conversation.

steps.do: A Markdown guide.
steps.do_zh: 一份 Markdown 手册
steps.expect: A Skill is one folder holding a SKILL.md file. It is prose instructions (plus optional scripts/assets) — not code that runs on its own. Kiro Crew ships many built-in ones (crystallize, web-browse, widgets, ...) and you can add your own.

You get a searchable list of every skill; each row carries a badge for how it loads — AUTO (always on), ON-DEMAND (loaded only when relevant), or POINTER (only its summary is shown until the agent opens it). Registry/package skills are grouped separately. On disk they live under ~/.kiro/crew/skills/, one folder per skill, but you rarely need to touch that directly.
steps.t: Browse skills in dashboard's Skills tab
steps.t_zh: 在 Skills 页浏览技能

steps.expect: (1) always: true → full content injected into every new session (the AUTO badge); (2) triggers match → full content injected when a trigger keyword appears in your message; (3) no match → only the one-line summary is shown (the POINTER badge (a normal skill with triggers carries ON-DEMAND instead — the badge is a fixed static class, not a per-message match state)), and the agent opens the full SKILL.md itself when it decides the skill is relevant.
steps.t_zh: 了解 Skills 加载方式

steps.do: Type its inline token — e.g. `$crystallize` — in your message.
steps.expect: That skill's full body is loaded for the turn. The agent can also find lesser-used skills with its skill_search tool.
steps.t: Pull a specific skill into chat
steps.t_zh: 在对话中调出指定 skill

steps.expect: Skills are read at runtime. Editing a skill in the Skills tab (the Edit button on a skill you own), or adding/removing one on disk, takes effect on the NEXT session — no `kirocrew` restart or package rebuild needed.

if_stuck.note: Ready to make one? See how to create a skill from the Skills tab.

entries.crew_prompt: Explain how Kiro Crew skills work: tell me which skills I currently have and, for two of them, their name, one-line description, and whether they are always-on or trigger-based. entries.title: Create a Skill in the Skills tab
entries.title_zh: 在 Skills 标签页创建 Skill
entries.symptom: You keep explaining the same procedure and want to save it as a reusable Skill.

steps.do: Click "Create new skill"
steps.do_zh: 点「Create new skill」
steps.expect: A form opens with fields for name, category (optional), description, triggers, tags, an "always" toggle, and the skill body. Nothing is written until you press Create.
steps.t_zh: 打开 dashboard 的 Skills 标签页

steps.do: Make it specific. Put your step-by-step instructions for the agent in the body
steps.expect: Name is the slug (e.g. my-skill). Description is the ONE line the LLM reads to decide when the skill is relevant. Only name and description are strictly required.
steps.t_zh: 填写技能身份和正文指令

steps.do: Leave "always" OFF for almost everything. Instead put comma-separated keywords in the triggers field. Prefix a keyword with `!` for a negative trigger
steps.do_zh: 也可选择常驻

The skill is written live under ~/.kiro/crew/skills/<slug>/SKILL.md and appears in the Skills list immediately — no rebuild. (This is a manual create, so it goes live directly; only auto-generated candidates wait in a review queue.)

steps.do: Start a NEW chat; type one of its trigger keywords, or `$<slug>`. Advanced: to scope a skill to one repo, select it, click Edit, and add `repo_scope: <relative/path>` to the frontmatter
steps.expect: Your skill's summary appears in the Available Skills list and its full body loads. It then loads only when that path exists in the session's project, and fails closed otherwise.
steps.t: Verify it loads in fresh session
steps.t_zh: 在新会话验证技能加载
