entries.crew_prompt: Help me author a new Kiro Crew skill. Ask me what task it should teach and what keywords should trigger it, then create the skill (name, a specific one-line description, always:false, comma-separated triggers, and clear step-by-step instructions in the body). Keep the description specific and under one line, and show me the result when done.

entries.title: Turn a session into a Skill with crystallize
entries.title_zh: 用 crystallize 把会话提炼成 Skill
entries.symptom: You solved something reusable and want to capture the procedure without writing SKILL.md by hand.

steps.do: In Kiro Crew.
steps.expect: (1) On-demand: you ask the agent to 'crystallize this' / 'save this as a skill'. (2) Automatic: when a session consolidates, a post-session pass can propose a skill from a successful procedure — governed by the toggle the Skills tab links as `skills.auto_create_from_sessions`. Both stage a CANDIDATE for human approval by default — nothing loads until you approve it.
steps.t: Know the two ways to create a Skill
steps.t_zh: 了解两种 Skill 生成方式

steps.do: Say 'crystallize this' (or 'create a skill' / 'make this reusable').
steps.expect: The agent reconstructs the working procedure (including any sub-agent results), checks for an existing near-duplicate skill to freshen instead, and stages a candidate under skills/auto/.pending/<slug>/ with SKILL.md + .meta.json.
steps.t: Ask the agent to crystallize the session
steps.t_zh: 让 agent 提炼当前会话

steps.do: Ask again and it will still capture it.
steps.expect: A skill must capture a procedure that RECURS on a different target. One-off work (a specific bug fix, a one-time audit, a planning chat) is not reusable even if it was long or hard. The agent will say so and name what makes it one-off — but the call is yours.

steps.do: In the dashboard's Skills tab. Click Review to read the full SKILL.md (and any bundled script) BEFORE approving. Approve to make it live and loadable (this also marks any bundled script executable), or Dismiss it.
steps.do_zh: 在 Skills 标签页里。
steps.expect: A Pending-review panel sits at the top when a candidate is waiting. Only 'create a LIVE skill' / 'create an ACTIVE skill' bypasses this queue — a plain 'create a skill' always stays a candidate.
steps.t_zh: 审阅并批准 Skill 候选

steps.do: (Optional) Force a session to consolidate and extract now; or just ask your Crew to run it. Use `kirocrew consolidate` to list sessions with unconsolidated messages, or `kirocrew consolidate --all` for all pending.
steps.do_zh: （可选）用于立刻强制某会话 consolidate 并提炼
steps.expect: This is a maintenance command with no dashboard equivalent. The named session consolidates immediately, which also triggers the auto-skill extraction pass.
steps.t: Run kirocrew consolidate with no args

if_stuck.note: If auto-extraction misses the point, create the skill by hand from the Skills tab instead.

steps.t_zh: 在 DM 获取面板链接

steps.do: Click the link within 5 minutes.
steps.expect: You get a link good for a 2-hour session. Durations are written as <N>h or <N>m and anything over 20 hours is quietly capped at 20h.
steps.t: Add a duration for a longer session

steps.do: Add a duration like `/kirocrew dashboard 30m` if you want.
steps.expect: Same result: a presigned dashboard link DM'd to you.
The app replies with a runtime stats summary (uptime, sessions, and so on). Other DM keywords work the same way: `cron list` shows scheduled jobs and `spawn <task>` runs a subagent.
steps.t: Check Crew status from the DM
steps.t_zh: 从 DM 检查 Crew 状态

if_stuck.note: Dashboard link showing 403? It usually means the token expired, your IP changed, or you opened it more than 5 minutes after it was issued — just run !dashboard again for a fresh link.

entries.crew_prompt: I'm using Kiro Crew from Slack. Please explain how to get a dashboard link with `!dashboard` (and `!dashboard 2h` for a longer session, or `/kirocrew dashboard`), and how to run keyword commands like `status`, `cron list`, and `spawn <task>` from a DM.

entries.title: Run parallel research with subagents, then synthesize it
entries.title_zh: 让子代理并行调研，再汇总结果
entries.symptom: You have independent items to research in parallel and want one synthesized answer.

steps.do: In plain English. You do NOT name a tool.
steps.do_zh: 使用自然语言。
steps.expect: Per the README: "Research these three options in parallel and recommend one" fans out to isolated subagents and synthesizes the tradeoffs. Kiro decides to delegate and calls the spawn_run MCP tool with a tasks=[...] list, one task per independent piece.

steps.do: In the Activity / Subagents panel.
steps.expect: One card per subagent shows its tool calls and progress live. All tasks in one batch spawn at once and run in parallel; the concurrency cap auto-sizes (floor 3), so a few tasks all start immediately.
steps.t: Watch subagents in the Activity panel
steps.t_zh: 在 Activity 面板查看 subagents

steps.expect: Each subagent's result is injected back into the SAME conversation as a `[Subagent completion event]` message. After a fan-out, one dedicated synthesis turn restates the goal, merges all results, and recommends next actions — you get a single answer, not N raw dumps. (spawn_run is fire-and-forget; the blocking sibling spawn_sub_agents returns the collected results inline instead.)

steps.do: Optional. Add `--async` to fire-and-forget: `kirocrew spawn run --async 'analyze logs'`. List active ones with `kirocrew spawn list`.
steps.do_zh: 此项可选。
steps.cmd: kirocrew spawn run 'check my open CRs'
steps.expect: Prints "Spawned subagent <id>, waiting for result..."then blocks and prints the result when done. `kirocrew spawn run --async 'analyze logs'` prints "Spawned subagent <id>: <task>"and returns immediately. `kirocrew spawn list` shows "No subagents."or lines like "<id> <task>"/ "<id> <task>".

entries.crew_prompt: I need to compare three approaches for X in parallel: (a) <option A>, (b) <option B>, (c) <option C>. Fan these out to separate subagents so they run at the same time, then synthesize the tradeoffs and recommend one. Bring the results back into this conversation.

if_stuck.note:
1. **Dashboard launch errors** — If `spawn_run`/`workflow_run` fails in dashboard chat with `'<urlopen error [Errno 111] Connection refused>'` or `'parent_session UNRESOLVED'`, the gateway is not down: the sandbox launch-hop runs dashboard chat in a credential-scrubbed network namespace.
2. **Migrated default agent** — Migrated users may also still have the default agent pinned to `priortool`; fix that first.
3. **Auto-sized subagent capacity** — Defaults and limits: auto-sizes from host memory/CPU, floored at 3 (ceiling `agent.subagent_auto_max`, default 32).
4. **Fixed capacity cap** — pin a fixed cap with `agent.max_subagents` (0 = auto, the default).
5. **Overflow queue timing** — Overflow queues and releases about every 2s.
6. **Nested subagents unsupported** — subagents cannot nest.
7. **Low free memory** — new spawns are refused below 4GB free memory (`agent.spawn_min_memory_gb`, set 0 to disable).
8. **Subagent turn limit** — 100 turns per subagent, configurable.

entries.title: When to use a subagent—and when to work inline
entries.title_zh: 什么时候用子代理，什么时候直接处理
entries.symptom: You are unsure whether to delegate; multiple steps alone are not a reason, and a lone subagent often adds overhead.

steps.do: Use this only when work splits into 2+ pieces (up to the auto-sized cap; overflow queues automatically) — they run concurrently. Keep dependent/sequential steps ordered, and never dispatch a step that needs a still-running subagent's result.
steps.do_zh: 仅适用于任务能拆成 2 个以上独立部分的情况（不超过自动调整的上限；超出部分会自动排队）——它们会并发运行。保持依赖/顺序步骤有序，绝不要派发依赖仍在运行的子代理结果的步骤。
steps.expect: Subagents shine on parallelism: independent reads, checks, or investigations that don't depend on each other's output.
steps.t: Delegate independent pieces in ONE spawn
steps.t_zh: 一次 spawn 委派独立任务

steps.do: This is also the one case a SINGLE subagent is worth it: to isolate a noisy investigation, or to route to a different model/specialist agent.
steps.do_zh: 这也是唯一值得使用单个子代理的情况：隔离嘈杂的调查，或路由到不同模型/专门代理。
steps.expect: A subagent absorbs a large file, a log dump, or a wide search and returns just the distilled result — your main context stays clean.
steps.t: Delegate to keep bulk data out
steps.t_zh: 委派任务以隔离大量数据

steps.do: Even when it has multiple steps, "Several steps" is NOT a reason to delegate. A little research then filing one ticket stays in the main session. A LONE subagent just running the whole task adds a round-trip and a context hop with zero parallelism gain — don't do it.
steps.do_zh: 即使任务有多个步骤，‘多个步骤’也不是委派的理由。少量调研后提交一个 ticket 仍应留在主会话中。让单个子代理包办整个任务只会增加一次往返和上下文跳转，却没有任何并行收益——不要这样做。

steps.do: Know the guardrails so expectations match reality: don't keep doing the work yourself in the same turn.
steps.do_zh: 了解硬约束，别有错误预期：不要在同一轮中继续自行完成这项工作。
steps.expect: Concurrency cap auto-sizes from host memory/CPU, floored at 3 (ceiling agent.subagent_auto_max, default 32). Each subagent has a 30-minute hard timeout and a per-run tool-call budget (default 100 turns). Results arrive as `[Subagent completion event]` messages.

entries.crew_prompt: I have this task: <describe it>. Tell me whether it's worth splitting across subagents or if you should just do it inline. If it fans out into independent pieces, spawn them in parallel; if it's simple or sequential, handle it directly and explain why.

entries.title: Hand Kiro Crew a task spec and walk away
entries.title_zh: 写一个 TASK.md 交给 Kiro Crew 自己跑
entries.symptom: You want a multi-step migration, refactor, or tested fix planned, run, verified, and reported without supervising each step.

steps.do: Save it as e.g. TASK.md. Write it goal-first: what to change, which files, and how success is checked (e.g. 'run pytest and fix failures').
steps.expect: Any nonempty text/Markdown file works. Markdown headings and a numbered '## Steps' list are a helpful convention, NOT a required schema; the runner sends the content to an LLM decomposer that derives the executable steps.

steps.do: In dashboard chat, just tell your Crew: "run the task in ./TASK.md" (or type the `run <path>` command). Or open the dashboard Tasks page, enter the spec file path, and click ▶ Start.
steps.expect: Either way it plans the steps, executes each in an isolated git branch (kirocrew/task/{task_id}), commits after each passed step, runs tests, and self-reviews the actual diff. Because it launches inside the gateway, any tool that isn't allow/deny-listed simply PROMPTS you interactively — no allowlist setup needed. Re-running the same spec auto-resumes from the last checkpoint.
steps.t: Start from chat or the Tasks page
steps.t_zh: 从聊天或 Tasks 页面启动

steps.do: Approve any tool prompt inline.
steps.expect: The dashboard shows each step with a status icon (planning → running → completed / failed / paused). A run can be paused, cancelled, or restarted from its saved plan right there on the Tasks page.

steps.do: Optional; headless is deny-by-default. Allowlist just the tools the task needs in ~/.kiro/crew/config.json under hooks.auto_approve_tools (e.g. ["read", "fs_write", "Running: pytest *"]) — avoid a blanket "*". Prefer the chat / Tasks-page path above unless you specifically need a headless run — or ask your Crew to set this up for you.
steps.do_zh: 可选；headless 默认拒绝工具。
steps.expect: Standalone `kirocrew run TASK.md` has NO interactive approval channel, so any tool not on the allowlist is rejected with reason: headless_no_authorization. Flags: --no-test skips per-step test verification, --timeout N caps total seconds (0 = none), --fresh ignores the checkpoint, --name overrides the task name.

if_stuck.note: If a step failed partway and you want to continue instead of restarting, see how checkpoints and resume work.

entries.crew_prompt: Help me use the Kiro Crew task runner. I have a spec file at ./TASK.md describing a multi-step change. Please review the spec, then start it — tell your Crew to "run the task in ./TASK.md" or launch it from the dashboard Tasks page so tool approvals prompt interactively. Watch the step-by-step progress and report which steps passed, failed, and the git branch it created. Only fall back to standalone `kirocrew run TASK.md` if I want a headless run; if a tool is then rejected as headless_no_authorization, tell me exactly which tools to add to hooks.auto_approve_tools in ~/.kiro/crew/config.json (scoped, not a blanket wildcard).

entries.title: Resume from a checkpoint—or start fresh
entries.title_zh: 从断点续跑，或重新开始
entries.symptom: A task stopped after a failure, pause, or gateway restart, and you want to continue without rerunning completed steps.

steps.do: Just start the same spec again — tell your Crew "run the task in ./TASK.md", click ▶ on the dashboard Tasks page, or run `kirocrew run TASK.md`.
steps.expect: Default behavior is auto-resume. It loads the saved checkpoint (runs.json + per-step git commits) and re-runs only the incomplete steps; anything already PASSED or SKIPPED is left alone. Progress survives restarts because runs are persisted to {work_dir}/runs.json.
steps.t: Relaunch the same spec to resume
steps.t_zh: 重新启动同一 spec 续跑

steps.do: To discard the partial work and re-run ALL steps from step 1, ask your Crew to "run ./TASK.md fresh, ignoring the checkpoint", or from a terminal use the --fresh flag: `kirocrew run TASK.md --fresh`. Use it when the earlier plan is stale or the partial work should be thrown away.
For a gateway-launched run open the dashboard Tasks page and click Execute / ↻ Restart on that project; watch for the tool prompt.
steps.expect: On gateway restart, any run still marked 'running' is automatically flipped to 'paused' (no zombie tasks). For a gateway-launched run there is no CLI 'resume' — it resets incomplete tasks to PENDING and continues. Note: a crash-recovered run always comes back with auto-approve OFF and requires an affirmative re-grant.

if_stuck.note: If you keep hitting the same failing step, the task may not be a good fit for unattended execution — see when to reach for the task runner vs. plain chat.

entries.crew_prompt: My Kiro Crew task at ./TASK.md stopped partway. Please check its status on the dashboard Tasks page (or via the `run status` command), tell me which steps passed vs. failed, and resume it from the last checkpoint by re-launching the spec — tell your Crew to "run the task in ./TASK.md" or click ▶ Restart on the Tasks page. Only do a fresh run (--fresh / "run it fresh") if you confirm the earlier work should be thrown away.

entries.title: When to use the task runner instead of just chatting
entries.title_zh: 什么任务适合用任务运行器（而不是直接聊天）
entries.symptom: You are choosing between normal chat, a monitor loop, and the structured task runner.

steps.do: For multi-step work.
steps.do_zh: 适用于多步骤工作。
steps.expect: Good fits: a migration, a refactor, a feature with tests, a fix-until-green loop — anything you can describe as ordered steps with a success check. The runner adds planning, per-step git commits + revert-on-failure, independent diff review, retries, replanning, checkpoint resume, and stall detection. Rule of thumb: 'do X and stop if the tests fail' is a task; 'help me think about X' is a chat.
steps.t: Use it for bounded verifiable work
steps.t_zh: 用于有边界可验证工作

steps.do: Use a normal chat for brainstorming, one-shot questions, exploratory back-and-forth, or work where you want to steer every step. For 'keep watching a PR/CI/deploy until a condition is met', use a monitor loop (monitor_start), not the task runner.
steps.do_zh: 适用于开放式或一次性工作。
steps.expect: Poor fits: brainstorming, one-shot questions, exploratory back-and-forth, or work where you want to steer every step.
steps.t: Use chat or a monitor loop

steps.do: For a step that must never run unattended (deploy, delete, push), mark it force_approval in the spec.
steps.do_zh: 让无人值守运行停下等待。
steps.expect: force_approval fails closed when there is no approval handler (e.g. standalone `kirocrew run`), so the task stops as failed rather than proceeding. requires_approval only prompts on the dashboard; without a handler it just warns and continues, so it is NOT a safe unattended gate.
steps.t_zh: 为不可逆步骤加审批闸

if_stuck.note: Decided it's a task? Go write the spec and run it.

entries.crew_prompt: I want to decide whether this piece of work should be a Kiro Crew task (kirocrew run TASK.md) or just a chat. Here is what I need to do: <describe the work>. Tell me which fits better and why, and if it's a task, draft a TASK.md spec with ordered steps, a success check, and force_approval on any irreversible step.

entries.title: Install and switch dashboard themes
entries.title_zh: 安装并切换仪表盘主题
entries.symptom: You want to change dashboard colors or install a full theme pack with fonts, branding, and an experience skin.

steps.do: In the dashboard go to Settings → Display.
steps.expect: You see ONE 'Theme' dropdown that lists the built-in themes plus any packs you have installed — a color theme and a full experience pack live in the same list.

steps.do: Pick any entry in the Theme dropdown. Install many.
steps.expect: The whole dashboard restyles right away; an 'Applying…' status shows briefly while it swaps. Only one is active at a time.

steps.do: Still in Settings → Display, use 'Install theme' and give it EITHER a local folder path OR an https github.com repo URL.
steps.expect: Install IS the validator: on success the pack appears in the Theme dropdown; on a bad pack the refusal message names exactly what to change (wrong level, oversized font, forbidden CSS, etc.).

steps.do: Re-install the same pack (same slug). Edit the pack SOURCE and re-install to iterate; do NOT hand-edit the installed copy under the data dir, because that bypasses validation.
steps.expect: Re-install OVERWRITES, that is the update path.
steps.t: Reinstall a pack to update it

if_stuck.note: A GitHub install can fail closed with code 'theme_install_sandbox_unavailable' on a host with no OS sandbox backend — clone the repo locally and install from the local folder path instead, which needs no sandbox.

entries.crew_prompt: Walk me through changing my Kiro Crew dashboard theme. Open Settings → Display, show me the Theme dropdown, and if I give you a local folder path or a github.com repo URL, install that theme pack for me and confirm it shows up in the dropdown. If the install is refused, tell me exactly what the pack needs fixed.

media.caption: Open Settings → Display, pick a theme and flip the mode — the whole dashboard reskins instantly.

entries.title: Give your bot a custom name
entries.title_zh: 给你的 bot 改个名字
entries.symptom: You want the assistant to use a custom name such as 'Jarvis' or 'Alita'.

steps.do: In dashboard chat, tell your Crew: "rename yourself to Jarvis" (or "set your bot name to Jarvis"). Ask it to set the name back to empty to return to the default.
steps.expect: It writes agent.bot_name into your config.json for you. The name is sanitized to letters, digits, spaces and _ - . and capped at 50 characters, so anything outside that set is stripped. (There is no dedicated Settings field for this — chat, or the terminal below, is the way to set it.)
steps.t: Tell your Crew its new name
steps.t_zh: 告诉 Crew 它的新名字

steps.do: Confirm with `kirocrew config get agent.bot_name` (it prints e.g. Jarvis). Set it to "" (empty) to return to the default name.
steps.expect: Same effect as asking your Crew: writes agent.bot_name into config.json.
steps.t: Set it yourself from a terminal

steps.do: Ask your Crew to restart the gateway for you, or run `kirocrew restart` yourself. Then start a NEW chat.
steps.expect: The gateway restarts and reloads config. The assistant now identifies with the name you set. (Existing sessions keep the old name until you start fresh.)
steps.t: Restart and open a new chat

if_stuck.note:
1. **Bot name changes only** — `bot_name` only changes the NAME the bot uses.
2. **Voice or branding changes** — To change its voice/tone or the dashboard branding (logo, avatar, fonts), that lives in the theme layer — a theme pack's `persona.md` sets tone (consent-gated) and its branding sets logo/wordmark.

entries.crew_prompt: I want to rename my Kiro Crew assistant to a custom name. Just set agent.bot_name to the name I give you (you can do it directly, or run `kirocrew config set agent.bot_name "<name>"`), confirm the value was saved, restart the gateway, and remind me to open a new chat so the new name takes effect.

entries.title: Pick your release channel: Stable, Insider, or Nightly
entries.title_zh: 选对更新渠道：Stable / Insider / Nightly
entries.symptom: You want early features or a calmer, more stable release channel.
entries.trust_note: Channels, cadence, and switch mechanics are the repo's own release reference; commands and URLs verified verbatim.

sources.label: docs/build/release.md → The three channels / Installing and switching channels

steps.do: Not its version number.
steps.do_zh: 不要只看版本号。
steps.expect: Stable = everyone (the default on every install path; ships Insider builds that baked long enough to be promoted). Insider = power users who want features days-to-weeks early and accept the new bugs. Nightly = us and contributors; untested `main` HEAD, expect breakage, rebuilt daily at 06:00 UTC.
steps.t: Choose a lane by how much churn

steps.do: For a CLI / one-line install.
steps.do_zh: 适用于 CLI / 一行安装。
steps.expect: Prints one word: `stable`, `insider`, or `nightly`. If the file is missing you're on the default, which is `stable`. (`KIROCREW_CHANNEL` overrides the recorded value.)

steps.do: For a CLI / one-line install. Substitute `nightly` or `stable` for `insider`.
steps.do_zh: 适用于 CLI / 一行安装。
steps.expect: Reinstalls from the chosen channel's feed and rewrites `~/.kiro/crew/channel`. The installer verifies the signed manifest before touching anything and rejects any channel name outside {nightly,insider,stable}.

steps.do: In Settings → About, flip the channel.
steps.expect: The other lane's current version then arrives as an ordinary in-app update. Nightly is different: it's a separate app with its own name and icon, so it installs alongside Stable/Insider rather than replacing them — but it reads the same `~/.kiro/crew` data unless you point it elsewhere with `KIROCREW_HOME`.
steps.t: Switch the desktop app between Stable and Insider
steps.t_zh: 在桌面版切换 Stable 与 Insider

steps.do: Re-run your container off the new tag to take it.
steps.expect: Multi-arch image (linux/amd64 + linux/arm64 under every tag, so the pull picks your architecture). Tags are `stable` / `insider` / `nightly` (plus `latest` for stable).
steps.t: Switch Docker channels by pulling another tag
steps.t_zh: 拉取其他 tag 切换 Docker 渠道

if_stuck.note: Already on the right channel and just want the latest bytes, or need to lock to one exact version? See updating & pinning.

entries.crew_prompt: I want to choose or switch my Kiro Crew release channel. Explain the difference between Stable, Insider, and Nightly for my use, tell me which channel my current install is on (check ~/.kiro/crew/channel for a CLI install, or Settings → About for the desktop app), and switch me to the channel I pick. For a CLI/one-line install, re-run the installer with `--channel <name>`. Confirm the new channel afterward.

entries.title: Update Kiro Crew — or pin it to one exact version
entries.title_zh: 升级 Kiro Crew —— 或钉死在某个具体版本
entries.symptom: You want the newest build, need to return to a known-good version, or must keep a fleet on one release.
entries.trust_note: Confirmed against the Kiro Crew release reference: the topbar 'Update Available' button runs the same update path as the CLI, and the pin and desktop auto-update behaviors are documented.

steps.expect: When a newer build is available, an "Update Available" button appears in the dashboard topbar. Clicking it runs the same refresh as the CLI update and then restarts the gateway for you — no terminal needed. This is the primary way to update whether you're on the desktop app, a browser dashboard, or a remote gateway.
steps.t: Click Update Available in dashboard topbar
steps.t_zh: 点击仪表盘顶栏 Update Available

steps.do: Desktop updates arrive automatically, but you can slow them down. The "autoDownloadUpdates" control is in Settings → About.
steps.do_zh: 桌面版会自动更新，但你可以放慢更新
steps.expect: The desktop app checks its channel feed 30s after launch, then every 4 hours (electron-updater), downloads updates automatically, and installs on your next quit (after gracefully stopping the gateway). An update you already declined then won't land on next quit, and nothing downloads until you click "Update Available" yourself.

steps.do: Re-run your installer, or run `kirocrew update` then `kirocrew restart`. You can also just tell your Crew "update my install" and it will run the right commands for how you installed.
steps.do_zh: 或让 Crew 代办。
steps.expect: A terminal install has no dashboard button that rebuilds it. Note: this refreshes your install in place; it does not switch your release channel.

steps.do: Re-run your installer with `--version <x.y.z>` (replace with the release you want) to install that exact immutable build through its pinned manifest rather than the moving channel feed — so the version can never drift under you. Combine with `--channel` if the version lives on insider or nightly. Your Crew can run this for you.
steps.expect: There's no dashboard control for pinning, so this stays a terminal step.
steps.t: Pin your install to one version

if_stuck.note: If updating pulled a build that behaves differently than you expected, you may be on a different release channel — check your channel and switch back by re-running your installer with its `--channel` flag.

entries.crew_prompt: Help me update Kiro Crew, or pin it to a specific version — UI-first. If a newer build is out, tell me to click "Update Available" in the dashboard topbar (it updates and restarts the gateway for me). If I'm on the Mac/Windows desktop app, explain that it auto-updates and how to turn off autoDownloadUpdates in Settings → About. For a terminal install, tell me to re-run my installer (or run `kirocrew update` then `kirocrew restart`) — or just do it for me. To lock an exact version, re-run the installer with `--version <x.y.z>` so it installs that immutable pinned build instead of the moving channel feed.

entries.title: Dictate to your Crew with a microphone
entries.title_zh: 用麦克风向 Crew 口述
entries.symptom: You want speech to appear as text in the message box instead of typing.

steps.expect: Settings has a Voice tab (mic icon) under Preferences. It has two sections: Text-to-Speech and Speech-to-Text — you want Speech-to-Text.

steps.do: In Speech-to-Text, flip the "Enabled" toggle (its description reads "Transcribe voice into the message box when you click the mic").
steps.expect: A "Status" row shows a green "ready" badge, or a "not installed" badge with the exact reason to fix if the recogniser or model isn't ready yet.

steps.do: For the local provider, pick a model, click the download button, and wait for the download progress to reach ready.
steps.do_zh: 本地 provider。
steps.expect: Provider defaults to "local". The Model row says "Models download on demand. Select one and click Download now; the desktop app already includes every other runtime dependency." Desktop builds bundle the recogniser; a non-desktop install needs the voice extra first (see next step). macOS Intel is the unsupported exception for the local provider.

steps.do: This applies if voice isn't ready; after it's installed, restart the gateway (Settings → About → Restart gateway) so it imports the new packages.
steps.do_zh: 语音未就绪时。
steps.expect: The voice extra provides the local whisper recogniser plus the AWS "transcribe" provider and browser/Slack voice decoding. Desktop builds bundle it already; other installs need the voice extra added for your edition — your Crew can do this for you.
steps.t_zh: 添加 voice 依赖并重启

steps.do: Optional.
steps.do_zh: 可选。
steps.expect: The "Microphone" dropdown lists your input devices.

steps.do: Back in chat, click the microphone icon in the message box and speak. Click the mic again to stop.
steps.expect: Words stream in as you talk (an animated Dictation panel, controlled by the "Dictation panel" toggle, shows while recording). The committed transcript stays in the box for you to edit or send.

if_stuck.note:
1. **Voice provider is missing** — 'Voice provider not installed' means speech-to-text is on but there's no local `whisper` (+ `ffmpeg`); the app auto-detects them in `~/.local/bin` or `PATH`.
2. **Set up remote host** — remote host (AL2023): `pip install --user openai-whisper` and drop a static ffmpeg into `~/.local/bin`.
3. **Set up on macOS** — macOS: `brew install openai-whisper ffmpeg`.
4. **Set up on Windows** — Windows: `winget install Gyan.FFmpeg` + `pip install openai-whisper`.
5. **Verify and restart tools** — Then `which whisper ffmpeg`, `kirocrew doctor`, `kirocrew restart`.
6. **Turn voice off** — If you don't want voice, just turn STT off in the dashboard Overview to clear the warning.
7. **Only System default shown** — If it only shows "System default", click "Allow microphone access to show device names" and grant the browser mic permission.

entries.crew_prompt: I want to dictate to you by voice instead of typing. Open Settings, go to the Voice tab, and walk me through enabling Speech-to-Text: turn on the Enabled toggle, pick and download a local model, and confirm the Status shows ready. If voice isn't available, tell me the voice extra needs to be present — the desktop app already bundles it, otherwise install the voice extra for my edition and restart the gateway. Then tell me how to click the mic in the composer to dictate.

entries.title: Hear your Crew reply aloud (text-to-speech)
entries.title_zh: 让 Crew 朗读回复（TTS）
entries.symptom: You want assistant replies spoken aloud with a local or cloud voice.

entries.title: SSH dashboard says 'Setup check unavailable'; WebSocket returns 403

entries.symptom: Over an SSH port-forward the dashboard shows 'Setup check unavailable' or 'Missing queryFn: ["kiro-prerequisite"]', and the WebSocket is rejected with 403 Forbidden.
entries.trust_note: The gateway builds an allowed-origin set from loopback plus the configured dashboard.url and enforces it on API/CSRF and the WebSocket upgrade, so a foreign tunnel origin is rejected (the UI then shows the missing 'kiro-prerequisite' query and a 403 WS).

steps.do: It's an origin-trust issue, not a Kiro CLI or token issue

steps.expect: The gateway only trusts requests whose Origin matches its known dashboard origins (loopback + a configured dashboard.url). steps.t_zh: 确认 origin 信任问题

steps.do: Then open http://localhost:5476 on your laptop.
steps.expect: A loopback origin is trusted by default, so the setup check runs and the WebSocket connects.
steps.t_zh: 使用 loopback 端口转发

steps.do: For a named host or tunnel. Use the exact scheme+host you actually browse to.
steps.do_zh: 若使用具名主机或隧道。
steps.expect: Sets the external origin the gateway will accept.

steps.expect: After the restart the setup check and WebSocket connect from that origin and the 403s stop.

if_stuck.note: Prefer the built-in tunnel / Remote Crew flow over a hand-rolled port-forward — it configures the trusted origin for you.

entries.title: Doctor's AWS account check fails with ExpiredToken

entries.trust_note: Kiro Crew never manages the AWS token itself — it resolves whatever the aws CLI's active profile provides via sts:GetCallerIdentity, so an expired SSO session has to be refreshed in the CLI, not in Kiro Crew.

sources.label: deploy/iam.py (aws sso login hint on unresolved profile)

steps.do: It belongs to AWS CLI, not Kiro Crew
steps.do_zh: 过期的是 AWS CLI token，不是 Kiro Crew
steps.expect: The step runs the equivalent of `aws sts get-caller-identity` under your default profile. ExpiredToken means that profile's SSO session lapsed; Kiro Crew just uses whatever the aws CLI resolves.
A browser opens to approve; on success the profile has a fresh token.
steps.t_zh: 刷新该 profile 的 SSO

steps.expect: Prints your account id, user id and ARN — no ExpiredToken.

steps.do_zh: 先跑 doctor。
steps.expect: The AWS account step is green.
steps.t: Re-run the cloud launcher and start the gateway
steps.t_zh: 重跑云启动器并启动 gateway

if_stuck.note:
Other red X marks in the doctor report are explained in the doctor guide.

If the profile was never set up, run `aws configure sso --profile <name>` first.

SSO sessions are short-lived, so this recurs routinely — just log in again when it does.
